Sarah laughed. "I don't think you can eat the whole thing, it's too big!" 

Lily grinned. "I can do it, just watch me!" 

So, Lily took a big bite of the cake. It was so delicious that she couldn't stop eating it. Soon, the whole piece was gone! "Wow, you did it!" Sarah exclaimed. "You're a great cake eater!" 

Lily smiled with pride. "Thanks, I love cake!"

Lily's mommy put the broken pieces of the bottle back together. She used glue to make it strong again. "There you go, Lily," her mommy said. "Your bottle is fixed."

Lily was happy to have her toy bottle back. She played with it all day long. And from that day on, she was very careful with her fragile toy bottle. And they lived happily ever after. The end.

In the end, the bird flew away with Zero and Tiny. They never got to play together again. Zero learned that being weird can be dangerous, and he wished he could go back to being with his friends.

Martin asked John to hold out his arm and said he had something special to give him. John held out his arm, expecting a toy. But instead, Martin took out a shirt. It was old, ripped, and very gross. John thought it was a bit disgusting.

Martin explained that he wanted John to have the shirt because it was special to him. Although John was a bit scared, he decided to accept the gift.

John thanked Martin, put on the shirt, and ran off to show it to his friends. From that day onwards, Martin and John became close friends and they still meet up in the park every weekend.

"Wow, this is the best hay ever!" she said to herself. "I am so lucky to have it all for me!"

But then, the hay started to move. It was too heavy for the pile to hold. The hay fell down, and Lily fell with it. She was buried under the hay, and she could not get out. She started to cry for help.

"Help! Help! I am stuck under the hay!" she shouted.

The other lambs heard her cry. They ran to the barn and saw what had happened. They felt sorry for Lily, but they also remembered how she never shared her hay with them.

"Why should we help you?" they asked. "You always ate all the hay by yourself. You did not care about us. You were greedy and selfish."

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Greediness and selfishness can lead to trouble and loneliness. Friendship and generosity can bring happiness and joy.

The car starts to make a loud noise. It is the alarm. It goes wooo wooo wooo. Ben and Tom are scared. They want to stop the alarm. They look for a button to turn it off. They see a big button with an R on it. They think it means "rest". They press it.

The car starts to move. It is not resting. It is reversing. It goes back and back and back. Ben and Tom scream. They do not know how to stop the car. They see a wall behind them. It is getting closer and closer. They hit the wall. The car makes a big crash. The alarm stops. The car is broken. The wall is broken. Ben and Tom are hurt.

Their dad hears the noise. He runs to the garage. He sees the car and the wall and the boys. He is very angry. He is also very sad. He has to pay a lot of money to fix the car and the wall. He has to take the boys to the doctor. He is bald, but he feels like he has lost more hair. He yells at Ben and Tom. He says they are very naughty and they cannot play with cars anymore. Ben and Tom cry. They are sorry. They wish they had not played with the big car. They wish they had listened to their dad. They have learned a hard lesson. The end.

Will was a wise boy who liked to notice things. He noticed the sun and the moon, the birds and the bugs, the flowers and the trees. He noticed when his mom was happy or sad, when his dad was busy or bored, when his sister was nice or mean. He noticed everything.

One day, he noticed a big box in the living room. It was wrapped with shiny paper and had a bow on top. He wondered what was inside. He asked his mom, "What is that?"

His mom smiled and said, "That is a surprise for you, Will. But you have to wait until your birthday to open it."

Will nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I will wait." But he was very curious. He wanted to know what was in the box. He thought maybe it was a toy, or a book, or a puzzle. He thought about it all day and all night.

The next day, he noticed that his mom and dad were busy in the kitchen. They were making a cake and blowing up balloons. He noticed that his sister was wearing a dress and had a ribbon in her hair. He noticed that his friends were coming over with gifts and cards. He realized that it was his birthday. He was very happy.

He ran to the living room and saw the big box. He said, "Can I open it now, mom?"

His mom said, "Yes, you can, Will. It is your special day. Go ahead and open it."

Will tore off the paper and the bow and opened the box. He gasped. Inside was a puppy. It was brown and white and had floppy ears. It wagged its tail and licked Will's face. Will hugged the puppy and said, "Thank you, mom and dad. Thank you, thank you, thank you. This is the best surprise ever. I love you, puppy."

His mom and dad said, "You're welcome, Will. We love you, too. Happy birthday, Will."

Will was a wise boy who liked to notice things. He noticed that he had a new friend, a new family member, a new adventure. He noticed that he was very lucky. He noticed that he was very happy.

She realized her mom was right. The party was fun. The green dress was pretty. The yellow dress was boring. She wished she had listened to her mom. She wished she had worn the green dress. She wished she had been a good girl.

Lily loved peanuts. She liked to eat them with her fingers and make crunch sounds. She also liked to share them with her friend Max, who was a squirrel. Max lived in a big tree near Lily's house. Every day, Lily would bring some peanuts to Max and they would play together.

One day, Lily found a big bag of peanuts in the kitchen. She was very happy. She thought she could take some to Max and have a lot of fun. She did not ask her mom or dad if she could have the peanuts. She just took the bag and ran outside.

She found Max on a branch and waved to him. "Max, Max, look what I have!" she shouted. "Peanuts, lots of peanuts! Come and get some!"

Max was very excited. He jumped down from the branch and ran to Lily. He grabbed a handful of peanuts and stuffed them in his mouth. He made happy noises and thanked Lily.

Lily smiled and opened the bag wider. She wanted to give Max more peanuts. But then she heard a loud voice behind her.

"Lily, what are you doing?" It was her dad. He looked angry and worried. "Those are not peanuts, they are nuts for the birds. They have salt and spices on them. They are not good for you or Max. You could get sick. Why did you take them without asking?"

Lily felt scared and sad. She did not know the nuts were for the birds. She did not know they had salt and spices. She did not want to get sick or make Max sick. She dropped the bag and started to cry.

"I'm sorry, dad, I'm sorry. I just wanted to give Max some peanuts. I like peanuts. I like Max. I did not mean to do something bad."

Her dad sighed and hugged her. He was not angry anymore, but he was still worried. He looked at Max, who was coughing and spitting out the nuts. He did not look happy.

"Max, I'm sorry too. I did not know Lily took the nuts. They are not good for you. You need to drink some water and eat some grass. Maybe you will feel better."

Max nodded and ran to a nearby fountain. He drank some water and ate some grass. He felt a little better, but he still had a bad taste in his mouth. He looked at Lily and her dad. He was not mad at them, but he was sad.

Lily and her dad walked to the fountain. They wanted to say sorry to Max again. They also wanted to give him some real peanuts, the ones that were perfect for him. They hoped he would forgive them and still be their friend.

They regretted taking the nuts for the birds. They learned to ask before they take something. They learned to be careful with what they eat and share. They learned to love peanuts and Max more.

One day, they went to a new place for their walk. It was a big hill with many colors. There were red, yellow, green, and blue patches on the hill. Lily and Ben wondered what they were.

"Mom, what are those colors?" Lily asked.

"They are plants, sweetie. They grow on the hill and make it look pretty," Mom said.

"Can we touch them?" Ben asked.

"No, honey. They are very delicate and we don't want to hurt them. We can look at them from here and enjoy the landscape," Dad said.

Lily and Ben nodded and looked at the colorful hill. They thought it was very beautiful and unusual. They wanted to see more of it.

They walked along the path that went around the hill. They saw more plants and animals. They saw a rabbit, a bird, a butterfly, and a lizard. They were happy and curious.

But then, they saw something that made them stop and gasp. It was a big hole in the hill. It was dark and deep and scary. Lily and Ben wondered what was inside.

"Mom, what is that?" Lily asked.

"Dad, can we go there?" Ben asked.

Mom and Dad looked at each other and smiled. They had a surprise for Lily and Ben.

"That, my dears, is a cave. And we are going to explore it," Mom said.

"A cave? What is a cave?" Lily asked.

"A cave is a place under the ground, where you can find many interesting things. Like rocks, crystals, water, and maybe even bats," Dad said.

"Bats? What are bats?" Ben asked.

"Bats are animals that fly at night. They are not scary, they are amazing. They use sound to find their way in the dark," Mom said.

Lily and Ben were excited and nervous. They wanted to see the cave and the bats, but they also felt a little afraid. They held their mom's and dad's hands and followed them to the hole.

Lily and Ben were amazed and happy. They had never seen anything like this before. They wondered what else they could find in the cave.

They said goodbye to the cave and the bats. They thanked them for letting them visit. They went back to the hole and climbed out.

They saw the hill and the colors again. They saw the sun and the sky. They felt warm and bright.

Behind the gate, there is a big dog. The dog is angry and loud. It has sharp teeth and claws. It does not like Tom and Sue. It runs towards them and barks. Tom and Sue are scared. They try to run back to the gate, but it is too late. The dog catches them and bites them. Tom and Sue cry and bleed. They wish they had listened to the sign. They wish they had not opened the gate.

Lily and Ben were very happy. They had a new pet. It was a hamster. They named it Fluffy. They wanted to play with Fluffy and give it food and water.

They brought Fluffy home in a cage. They put the cage on the table. They wanted to unpack Fluffy and let it run in the house. They opened the cage door.

"Come on, Fluffy, come out!" Lily said. She was enthusiastic. She reached her hand inside the cage.

But Fluffy was scared. It did not want to come out. It bit Lily's finger. Lily screamed. She pulled her hand out of the cage.

"Ow, ow, ow! Fluffy bit me!" Lily cried. She ran to her mom. She showed her finger. It was bleeding.

Ben was angry. He did not like Fluffy anymore. He grabbed the cage. He threw it out of the window.

"Bad Fluffy! Go away!" Ben shouted. He did not care about Fluffy.

The cage fell on the ground. It broke. Fluffy ran out of the cage. It was free. But it was also alone. It did not know where to go. It was cold and hungry. It saw a big cat. The cat saw Fluffy. The cat chased Fluffy. Fluffy tried to run away. But it was too late. The cat caught Fluffy. Fluffy was gone.

The end.

Sam says, "Wow, that is nice. Can I see your letter?" He reaches for the letter, but Tom pulls it away. He says, "No, it is mine. You cannot have it. Go away."

Sam feels sad and angry. He wants to see the letter too. He thinks Tom is not a good friend. He says, "Fine, I do not want to play with you. You are mean." He runs away and bumps into a tree. He falls down and hurts his knee. He cries out loud.

Tom hears Sam crying. He feels sorry for him. He remembers that Sam is his friend. He runs to him and says, "Are you okay, Sam? I am sorry I was mean. You can see my letter if you want. Here, take it."

Sam stops crying. He looks at the letter. He sees the stickers and the candy. He smiles and says, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend. I am sorry I ran away. Can I share the candy with you?"

Tom nods and says, "Yes, of course. Let us share the candy and the stickers. And let us play with the cars and the balls. We can have fun together."

They hug and make up. They eat the candy and stick the stickers on their cars and balls. They play and laugh. They are happy. They have a letter, a hurt knee, and a friendship.

Tom and Lily were playing pirates in the garden. They had a big box that they pretended was their ship. They also had a map that showed them where to find treasure.

"Look, the map says we have to dig here!" Tom said, pointing to a spot under a tree.

"Okay, let's dig!" Lily said, grabbing a shovel.

They dug and dug until they hit something hard. They pulled it out and saw that it was a metal box with a lock.

"Wow, we found the treasure!" Tom exclaimed.

"Let's open it!" Lily said, trying to break the lock.

But the lock was too strong and they could not open it.

"Maybe we need a key," Tom said.

"Or maybe we need to say a magic word," Lily said.

They tried different words, but nothing worked.

Then they heard a voice behind them.

"Hey, what are you doing with my box?" It was Mr. Brown, the old man who lived next door. He was deaf and could not hear very well.

"This is our treasure, we found it!" Tom said.

"No, it's not, it's mine! I buried it here a long time ago. It has my old toys and photos inside," Mr. Brown said.

He walked over and took the box from them.

"Please, can we see what's inside?" Lily asked.

"No, you can't, it's private. Go away and leave me alone," Mr. Brown said.

He turned around and walked back to his house.

Tom and Lily were sad and angry. They wanted to see the treasure.

"Let's follow him and sneak into his house," Tom said.

"No, that's not nice, that's rude. We should say sorry and ask him nicely," Lily said.

She insisted that they should be polite and respectful.

Tom thought for a moment. He knew that Lily was right.

"Okay, let's do that," he said.

They ran after Mr. Brown and knocked on his door.

"Mr. Brown, Mr. Brown, please open the door," they shouted.

Mr. Brown opened the door and looked at them.

"What do you want?" he asked.

"We want to say sorry for taking your box. We didn't know it was yours. We thought it was treasure," Tom said.

"Yes, we're sorry. And we also want to ask you if you can show us what's inside. We're curious and we like old toys and photos," Lily said.

Mr. Brown looked at them and saw that they were sincere and friendly.

He smiled and said, "Well, okay, I guess I can show you. But you have to be careful and not touch anything. Come in, come in."

He invited them into his house and opened the box.

Tom and Lily saw many interesting things inside. There were toy cars and dolls and books and puzzles. There were also photos of Mr. Brown when he was young and happy.

"Wow, this is amazing!" Tom said.

"Yes, this is really cool!" Lily said.

They asked Mr. Brown questions about his toys and photos. He told them stories and jokes. They laughed and had fun.

They realized that Mr. Brown was not mean and grumpy. He was lonely and sad.

They decided to be his friends and visit him often.

They also learned that sometimes, the best treasure is not something you find, but someone you meet.

But Tommy does not like to bathe. He does not like to get wet and soapy. He does not like to wash his hair and face. He does not like to wear his pajamas.

He says, "Okay, Mommy, I will bathe. But only for a little bit. And only if you stay with me. And only if I can have a story after."

Sam was a poor boy who lived in a small house with his mom and dad. He had only one sock that he wore on his left foot. His right foot was always cold and dirty. He wished he had another sock, but his mom and dad had no money to buy him one.

One day, he saw a big truck outside his house. It had many boxes and bags on it. Sam was curious and wanted to see what was inside. He crawled under the fence and ran to the truck. He climbed on it and opened a box. He saw many things that he had never seen before: toys, books, clothes, and shoes. He was so happy and excited. He wanted to take something for himself.

He saw a pair of socks that looked soft and warm. They were blue and had stars on them. He thought they would fit his feet perfectly. He grabbed them and put them in his pocket. He was about to climb down from the truck when he heard a voice.

"Hey, kid, what are you doing there?" It was the driver of the truck. He was a big man with a beard and a hat. He looked angry and scary.

Sam was afraid and tried to run away. But the driver caught him by his shirt and pulled him down. He took the socks from his pocket and threw them on the ground.

"These are not yours, kid. These are for the orphanage. You are a thief and a liar. Go away and don't come back!" He shouted at Sam.

Sam felt ashamed and sad. He crawled away from the truck and ran back to his house. He cried and hugged his mom. He told her what happened and said he was sorry.

His mom was kind and gentle. She kissed his head and said, "It's okay, Sam. I know you were just curious and wanted something nice. But you can't take things that don't belong to you. That's wrong and hurtful. You have to be honest and respectful. Maybe someday, someone will give you a pair of socks as a gift. But until then, you have to be happy with what you have. You have me and dad, and we love you very much. That's more than many kids have."

Sam nodded and smiled. He felt better and hugged his mom back. He said, "I love you too, mom. You are the best mom in the world. And I don't need socks. I have you."

Tom was a cat who liked to play with yarn. He had a big ball of blue yarn that he found in the closet. He rolled it, chased it, and scratched it. He had so much fun with his blue yarn.

One day, he saw another ball of yarn in the closet. It was red and shiny. Tom wanted to play with it too. He left his blue yarn on the floor and jumped to the red yarn. He rolled it, chased it, and scratched it. He had so much fun with his red yarn.

But then, he heard a loud noise. It was his owner, Lisa. She came into the closet and saw the mess. She saw the blue yarn and the red yarn all tangled and ripped. She was angry. She scolded Tom and took away both balls of yarn. She said, "Tom, you are a bad cat. You cannot have two balls of yarn. You have to share and take care of your things. You cannot change your mind all the time. You have to be happy with what you have."

Tom felt sad and sorry. He realized he made a mistake. He wished he had not left his blue yarn. He wished he had not played with the red yarn. He wished he had listened to Lisa. He looked at his paw and saw a bit of blue yarn stuck to his claw. He remembered how much he loved his blue yarn. He wanted it back.

He went to Lisa and rubbed his head against her leg. He meowed softly and looked at her with his big eyes. He tried to say he was sorry and he wanted his blue yarn. Lisa saw his paw and understood. She smiled and hugged him. She said, "Tom, I forgive you. You are a good cat. You learned your lesson. You can have your blue yarn back. But you have to promise me you will not play with the red yarn again. You have to be loyal and grateful to your blue yarn. It is your friend."

Tom nodded and purred. He was happy and thankful. He took his blue yarn and played with it gently. He never looked at the red yarn again. He learned to be happy with what he had. He learned to not change his mind all the time. He learned to be loyal and grateful to his friend. He learned a moral value.

"I don't know," Lily says. She looks at the mark. "Maybe it is dirt."

Lily follows him. She is curious.

In the bathroom, Ben fills the sink with water. He puts the sheep in the water. He rubs the wool with his hands. He tries to wash off the mark.

Tim and Sue ran to the boy and the girl and introduced themselves. The boy and the girl smiled and said their names were Ben and Liz. They said they lived in a small hut near the park, and they did not have many things, but they liked to make their own toys and games.

"Can we play with your ball and stick?" Tim asked.

"Sure, you can, but you have to measure how far you can throw the ball," Ben said. "We like to see who can throw the farthest."

"Okay, that sounds fun," Sue said. "How do you measure?"

"We use our feet," Liz said. "We count how many steps it takes to reach the ball."

They took turns throwing the ball and measuring the distance. Tim and Sue were surprised that Ben and Liz could throw very far, even though they were smaller than them. They also learned how to make other toys and games with sticks, stones, leaves, and flowers. They had a lot of fun, and they forgot about the time.

"Tim, Sue, it's time to go home," their mom called. "Say goodbye to your new friends."

Tim and Sue hugged Ben and Liz and thanked them for playing with them. They said they hoped to see them again soon.

"Bye, Tim and Sue," Ben and Liz said. "You are very nice and friendly. We are glad we met you."

Tim and Sue waved and followed their mom to the car. They felt happy and grateful for their new friends. They realized that being wealthy was not only about having many things, but also about having a good heart. They wondered what other adventures they would have in the park.

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the park together. One day, they saw a big fountain with water and lights. It was very pretty.

"Let's go see the fountain!" Lily said.

"OK!" Ben said.

They ran to the fountain and watched the water go up and down. They saw some coins in the water. People threw them to make a wish.

"Can we throw a coin too?" Lily asked.

"Sure!" Ben said. He had a coin in his pocket. He gave it to Lily.

"Thank you, Ben!" Lily said. She closed her eyes and made a wish. She threw the coin in the water.

"What did you wish for?" Ben asked.

"I wished for a puppy!" Lily said. "I want a puppy so much. A puppy is loyal and cute and fun."

Ben felt sad. He wanted a puppy too, but he did not have a coin. He looked around and saw a coin on the ground. It was shiny and new. He picked it up.

"Look, Lily, I found a coin!" Ben said.

"Wow, lucky you!" Lily said. "What are you going to wish for?"

Ben looked at the coin and then at Lily. He had to decide. He could wish for a puppy too, or he could wish for something else. He thought about what he wanted most.

He smiled and said, "I wish for you to be happy, Lily. You are my best friend."

He threw the coin in the water and hugged Lily.

"Thank you, Ben!" Lily said. "You are my best friend too. You are very loyal and kind and sweet."

They watched the fountain together and felt happy. They did not need a puppy. They had each other.

Lila and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a big sack full of different things: cars, dolls, blocks, books, and more. They liked to dump the sack on the floor and make up stories with their toys.

"Look, this is a rocket," Ben said, holding a red car. "It can fly to the moon and the stars and the universe."

"What is the universe?" Lila asked, curious.

"The universe is everything that is out there, far, far away. It has many colors and shapes and lights. It is very big and beautiful," Ben explained.

"Wow, I want to see the universe," Lila said, impressed.

"Maybe we can go there someday, if we find a real rocket," Ben said, smiling.

They pretended to fly their car to the universe, making zooming noises and waving to the planets. They had a lot of fun.

"Time for a break, kids. Come and eat something," Mom said, putting the tray on the table.

Lila and Ben ran to the table, hungry. They each took a sandwich and a piece of apple. They also dipped a carrot in the salsa.

"Careful, the salsa is spicy," Mom warned.

Lila and Ben took a bite of the carrot with salsa. They felt a hot and tangy sensation in their mouths. They made funny faces and reached for their water.

"Spicy, spicy!" they shouted, laughing.

Mom laughed too. She gave them a hug and a kiss.

"Spicy is good, but not too much. You are brave to try new things. Just like explorers of the universe," she said.

Lila and Ben smiled. They liked spicy and they liked the universe. They finished their snacks and went back to their toys. They still had many stories to tell.

Tom and Mia liked to play with cardboard. They had many boxes and tubes and cut them into shapes. They made a castle, a rocket, a boat and a train. They had fun pretending to be kings, astronauts, pirates and drivers.

One day, they found a big cardboard box in the garage. It was very tough and hard to cut. Tom and Mia wanted to make a car out of it. They asked their dad for help. He gave them scissors, tape and markers. He said, "Be careful with the scissors. They are sharp. And don't cut yourself."

Tom and Mia started to cut the box. They made holes for the windows and the doors. They taped some tubes for the wheels and the exhaust. They drew lights, mirrors and a number plate. They were very proud of their car.

They took their car outside and put it on the grass. They got inside and pretended to drive. They made noises like "vroom, vroom" and "beep, beep". They had a lot of fun.

But then, a big dog came running. It saw the car and thought it was a toy. It barked and jumped on the car. It bit the cardboard and tore it apart. Tom and Mia were scared and angry. They shouted, "No, no, go away! That's our car!"

They tried to resist the dog. They pushed it and pulled it. They threw sticks and stones. But the dog was stronger and faster. It ruined their car. It left holes and scratches and pieces everywhere.

Tom and Mia cried. They ran back to the garage. They hugged their dad. He said, "I'm sorry, kids. That was a bad dog. It didn't know any better. Don't worry, we can make another car. We have more cardboard. And this time, we'll make it tougher."

Tom and Lily were so happy. They hugged their dad and ran to the boat. They put on their life jackets and got on the boat. Their dad started the engine and the boat began to move on the sea.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys in the garden. They had a castle, a king, a queen, a dragon and some knights. They liked to make up stories with their toys and act them out.

One day, they decided to play a story where the dragon was angry and wanted to take the king away. The king was scared and hid in the castle. The queen and the knights tried to stop the dragon, but the dragon was too big and strong. He breathed fire and knocked down the walls.

"Oh no, what can we do?" the queen cried.

"We need to solve this problem," Ben said. He was playing the role of the knight leader. "We need to find a way to make the dragon happy and leave the king alone."

Lily thought for a moment. She was playing the role of the queen. She looked at the dragon and noticed something. The dragon had a long, flexible tail that he liked to swing around. She had an idea.

"Maybe the dragon is bored and lonely," she said. "Maybe he just wants to play. Look, he has a flexible tail. Maybe we can play with his tail and make him laugh."

Ben liked Lily's idea. He picked up a rope and tied it to the end of the dragon's tail. He pulled the rope and made the tail move like a snake. The dragon looked surprised and curious. He followed the rope with his eyes and tried to catch it with his mouth.

Lily picked up a ball and threw it to the dragon. The dragon caught the ball with his tail and threw it back to Lily. He made a loud, happy noise. He liked playing with the rope and the ball.

The king saw that the dragon was not angry anymore. He came out of the castle and thanked the queen and the knights for solving the problem. He invited the dragon to join them for a tea party. The dragon agreed and became their friend.

Ben and Lily smiled and hugged each other. They were happy that they solved the problem and made a new friend. They continued to play with their toys and had a lot of fun.

Mia and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big, furry dog with a long tail. The dog is friendly and wags its tail. Mia and Ben want to pet the dog, but they have to ask the owner first.

"Can we touch your dog, please?" Mia asks the lady with the dog.

"Sure, you can. His name is Spot. He likes children. But be gentle, okay?" the lady says.

Mia and Ben nod and go to the dog. They stroke his fur and scratch his ears. Spot licks their faces and makes them giggle. He is very soft and warm.

But then, Ben sees something shiny on the dog's collar. It is a tag with the dog's name and address. Ben likes shiny things. He tries to grab the tag, but the dog does not like it. He pulls his head away and growls.

"Ben, no! Don't do that!" Mia says. "You are hurting the dog. He does not want you to take his tag. It is his, not yours."

But Ben does not listen. He wants the tag. He tries to pull it off the dog's collar. The dog resists. He barks and snaps at Ben. Ben gets scared and lets go. He starts to cry.

The lady and Mia run to Ben. They check if he is okay. He is not hurt, but he is very upset.

"I'm sorry, I'm sorry," the lady says. "Spot is usually very nice, but he does not like anyone touching his tag. It is his special thing. He thinks you are trying to take it away from him."

"It's okay, it's okay," Mia says. "Ben did not know. He likes shiny things. He did not mean to make the dog angry. He is sorry, too."

Ben nods and wipes his tears. He looks at the dog. The dog looks at him. They are both calm now.

"Can I say sorry to the dog?" Ben asks.

"Of course you can," the lady says. "But be careful. Don't touch his tag. Just say sorry and give him a pat."

Ben does what the lady says. He goes to the dog and says, "Sorry, Spot. I did not want to hurt you. You are a good dog. You have a nice tail and a nice fur."

The dog wags his tail and licks Ben's hand. He forgives him. Ben smiles and pets the dog. Mia joins them. They all hug the dog. The dog is happy. He likes Mia and Ben. They are his new friends.

But then, a man comes to the bench. He looks angry and sad. He sees the camera in Sara's hand.

"Uh-oh, what's that?" Tom asked.

"I don't know, but it smells bad!" Anna said.

They ran out of the kitchen and saw a fire truck outside. A fireman knocked on the door and opened it. He saw the smoke and the cake in the oven. He turned off the oven and took out the cake. It was black and hard and smelled awful.

"Who baked this cake?" the fireman asked.

Tom and Anna looked at each other and felt uncomfortable. They knew they had done something wrong.

"We did, sir," Tom said.

"We wanted to surprise our mom," Anna said.

The fireman smiled and said, "That's very sweet of you, but you should never bake without an adult. Baking can be dangerous if you don't watch the oven. Next time, ask your mom or dad to help you, okay?"

Tom and Anna nodded and said, "Okay, sir. We're sorry."

The fireman said, "It's okay, no one got hurt. But this cake is not edible. How about I help you make a new one? I know a good recipe."

Tom and Anna smiled and said, "Yes, please!"

The fireman took them to his fire truck and showed them his kitchen. He had some ingredients and tools in a box. He taught them how to measure, mix, and bake a cake. He also let them decorate it with frosting and sprinkles. The cake looked and smelled delicious.

"Wow, you're a great baker, sir!" Tom said.

"Thank you, you're great helpers!" the fireman said.

They wrapped the cake in a paper and wrote a note for their mom. They thanked the fireman and gave him a hug. He drove them back to their house and said goodbye.

Tom and Anna ran inside and put the cake on the table. They waited for their mom to come home. When she saw the cake and the note, she was very happy and proud. She hugged them and said, "This is the best cake ever! Thank you, my loves!"

They cut the cake and shared it with their mom and the fireman. They all enjoyed it and had a fun time. Tom and Anna learned a lesson and made a new friend. They never baked without an adult again.

Mom heard them and smiled. She wanted to have some fun too. She put some spaghetti on a plate and sneaked into the living room. She hid behind the couch and waited.

Lily and Tom did not see her. They kept playing. Lily roared like a lion and Tom chattered like a monkey. They ran towards the couch.

Mom jumped out and shouted, "Boo!" She held the plate of spaghetti in front of her face. She made a funny noise.

Lily and Tom were scared. They screamed and ran away. They thought Mom was a spaghetti monster.

Mom laughed and said, "It's me, it's me! I was just joking. Come here, my little animals. It's time for dinner."

Lily and Tom stopped and looked at Mom. They saw her face and the spaghetti. They realized it was a prank. They felt silly and laughed too.

They hugged Mom and said, "You scared us, Mom. But we love you. And we love spaghetti."

Mom said, "I love you too. And I'm glad you love spaghetti. Let's go to the kitchen and eat. Maybe we can have some ice cream later."

Lily and Tom were happy. They followed Mom to the kitchen. They ate spaghetti and ice cream. They had a good time. They were not scared anymore. They were glad.

Lily and Tom were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a new path in the park. It was dark and dirty.

"Let's go there," Tom said. "Maybe we can find something fun."

Lily was frightened. She did not like the new path. She saw big bugs and old cans. She smelled something bad.

"No, Tom, let's not go there," Lily said. "It looks scary. Maybe there is something that can hurt us."

Tom did not listen. He wanted to see more. He ran into the new path. Lily followed him. She did not want to be alone.

They walked and walked. The new path was long and twisted. They did not see the park anymore. They only saw more dark and dirty things. They heard strange noises.

"Tom, I want to go back," Lily said. "I don't like it here. I'm scared."

Tom did not answer. He was looking at something on the ground. It was a big bag. It was brown and wet. It had holes in it.

"Look, Lily, what's in here?" Tom said. He opened the bag.

Lily screamed. She saw what was in the bag. It was a dead cat. It was rotting. It had no eyes. It had worms on it.

Tom screamed too. He dropped the bag. He tried to run away. But he slipped on the wet ground. He fell on the rotting cat. The worms crawled on him.

Lily ran away. She cried for help. She wanted to find the park. She wanted to find her mom. She wanted to forget what she saw.

But she could not. She could still see the rotting cat. She could still hear Tom's scream. She could still smell the bad smell.

She was lost. She was alone. She was frightened.

One day, they find a big tube in the garage. It is green and shiny. Anna wants to play with it. She says, "This is my tube. I can fit inside it. It is fun."

Ben wants to play with it too. He says, "No, this is my tube. I can fit inside it too. It is mine."

They both try to fit inside the tube at the same time. They push and pull and squeeze. But the tube is too small for both of them. They get stuck in the tube. They cannot move. They feel sad and angry.

They start to cry and shout. They make a lot of noise. They say, "Help! Help! Get us out of here!"

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the garage. She sees Anna and Ben in the tube. She says, "Oh, no! What have you done? You are both in trouble. You have to share the tube. You cannot be selfish."

She pulls the tube and frees Anna and Ben. They come out of the tube. They are red and sweaty. They say, "Sorry, Mom. Sorry, Anna. Sorry, Ben."

Mom says, "It's okay. I'm glad you are safe. But next time, you have to ask before you take something. And you have to take turns and play nicely. Do you understand?"

Anna and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, Mom. We understand. We will share the tube. We will be friends."

Mom smiles. She says, "Good. Now, go and wash your faces. Then you can play with the tube again. But be careful and have fun."

Anna and Ben hug Mom. They say, "Thank you, Mom. We love you."

They go and wash their faces. Then they go back to the garage. They play with the tube again. But this time, they take turns and fit inside it one by one. They make shapes and tunnels. They laugh and have fun. They are happy.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play and learn together. One day, they have to do some work for school. They have to draw a picture of their favorite animal.

Lily loves cats. She draws a big cat with soft fur and green eyes. She is very proud of her work. She shows it to Tom.

"Wow, Lily, your cat is very nice. You are very intelligent," Tom says.

Tom loves dogs. He draws a small dog with brown spots and a wagging tail. He is not very happy with his work. He thinks his dog is ugly. He does not show it to Lily.

Lily asks, "Tom, can I see your dog? I am sure it is very nice too."

Tom feels shy. He does not want Lily to see his dog. He covers his work with his hand.

"No, Lily, you cannot see my dog. It is very bad. I am not intelligent," Tom says.

Lily feels sad. She wants to help Tom. She says, "Tom, please do not cover your work. Let me see your dog. I am your friend. I will not laugh at you. I will help you."

Tom trusts Lily. He moves his hand and shows his work to Lily.

Lily smiles. She says, "Tom, your dog is very nice. You are very intelligent. You just need to practice more. Look, I can show you how to make your dog better. You can add some ears, a nose, and a collar. Then your dog will look more like a real dog."

Tom listens to Lily. He follows her advice. He adds some ears, a nose, and a collar to his dog. He sees that his dog looks better. He feels happy.

"Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. You are a good friend. I like your cat and your dog," Tom says.

Lily and Tom hug. They are happy. They have finished their work. They have learned something new. They have helped each other.

The moral of the story is: Do not be afraid to show your work. Do not be ashamed of your mistakes. Do not cover your work. Ask for help when you need it. Help others when you can. Be kind and friendly. You are intelligent. You can learn and improve.

Tom was a rabbit who liked to eat celery. He ate celery every day for breakfast, lunch and dinner. He liked the green and crunchy celery very much. He did not like to share his celery with anyone.

One day, Tom saw a big and yellow carrot in the garden. He thought the carrot looked very tasty. He wanted to try the carrot. He left his celery behind and ran to the carrot. He did not see the trap that the farmer had set.

The trap snapped on Tom's leg and hurt him a lot. He cried and cried, but no one came to help him. He was stuck in the trap. He could not move. He could not eat. He could not go back to his celery.

He looked at his celery and felt very sad. He wished he had not left his celery. He wished he had shared his celery with his friends. He missed his celery and his friends. He learned that celery was better than carrot, and sharing was better than being greedy.

But it was too late. The farmer came and took Tom away. He put Tom in a cage and sold him to a pet shop. Tom never saw his celery or his friends again. He had a bad ending.

Tom and Lily were scared. They saw a woman with a long nose, a pointy hat and a black dress. She was a witch!

Sam feels sad and angry. He says, "No, that is my monkey. Give it back. It is not yours." He tries to grab Mimi, but the big boy is stronger. He pushes Sam away and runs.

Sam cries and shouts. He makes a loud noise. His mom and dad hear him and come to him. They ask him what is wrong. He tells them about the big boy and Mimi.

His mom and dad hug him and say, "We are sorry, Sam. That was not nice of the big boy. He should not take things that are not his. We will help you find Mimi. Don't worry."

They look for the big boy and Mimi. They see them near the swings. The big boy is still holding Mimi. He is not playing with it. He is just holding it.

Sam's dad goes to the big boy and says, "Excuse me, son. That monkey belongs to Sam. He loves it very much. He did not mean to leave it on the bench. He was just playing on the slide. Can you please give it back to him?"

The big boy looks at Sam's dad and then at Sam. He sees that Sam is sad and wants Mimi. He feels a little sorry. He says, "Okay, fine. Here is your monkey. I don't really like it anyway. It is too small and soft."

He gives Mimi back to Sam. Sam is happy. He hugs Mimi and says, "Thank you, thank you. I missed you, Mimi. You are my best friend."

He also says, "Thank you, dad. You are very brave and kind. You helped me get Mimi back."

Sam's dad smiles and says, "You are welcome, Sam. I am proud of you. You stood up for yourself and your monkey. You are brave and kind, too."

Sam's mom says, "Yes, you are, Sam. And you are also very smart and sweet. We love you very much."

They all hug and kiss. They go back to the bench and have a snack. They share it with Mimi. They have a good time at the park. They are a happy family.

But one day, Lily had no one to perform for. Her mom and dad were busy working. Her big brother was at school. Her baby sister was sleeping. Lily felt sad and bored. She did not want to play with her toys or read her books. She wanted to perform.

She had an idea. She took her phone and called her grandma. She said, "Hi, grandma. Can I perform for you?" Grandma said, "Of course, my sweetie. I would love to see your show." Lily smiled and said, "Okay, grandma. Watch me."

She put her phone on the table and started her show. She sang her favorite song and danced and jumped and spun on the rug. She made funny faces and told jokes. Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a pond with ducks and fish. Lily wants to feed the ducks. Ben wants to catch the fish.

"I have bread for the ducks," Lily says. "They are hungry and nice."

"I have a net for the fish," Ben says. "They are fast and fun."

Lily and Ben disagree. They do not want to do the same thing. They get angry and say mean words.

"You are stupid," Lily says. "Ducks are better than fish."

"You are stupid," Ben says. "Fish are better than ducks."

They stop being friends and go to different sides of the pond. They do not talk or play.

A big dog comes to the park. He sees the bread and the net. He thinks they are toys. He runs to the pond and grabs them. He makes a mess and scares the ducks and the fish.

Lily and Ben see the dog. They are sad and scared. They want their bread and their net back. They do not like the dog.

They run to each other and hug. They say sorry and nice words.

"You are not stupid," Lily says. "Ducks and fish are both good."

"You are not stupid," Ben says. "We can share the bread and the net."

They become friends again and play together. They feed the ducks and watch the fish. They do not disagree. They are happy.

"Look at my cat!" Mia said. "She has whiskers and a tail."

"Look at my snake!" Leo said. "He can slither and hiss."

They were having fun with their yarn. But then they saw a big ball of yarn on the shelf. It was red and soft and shiny. They both wanted the ball of yarn.

"I want the ball of yarn!" Mia said.

"No, I want the ball of yarn!" Leo said.

They both reached for the ball of yarn. They pulled and tugged and fought over the ball of yarn. The ball of yarn did not like being pulled and tugged and fought over. It rolled off the shelf and bounced on the floor. It rolled out of the door and down the stairs. It rolled out of the house and into the street.

Mia and Leo ran after the ball of yarn. They did not see the car coming. The car was fast and loud and scary. The driver saw the ball of yarn and the children. He pressed the brake and honked the horn. He hoped they would stop and yield.

But Mia and Leo did not stop and yield. They were too busy chasing the ball of yarn. They did not hear the car or the horn. They did not see the danger. They only saw the ball of yarn.

The driver swerved and missed the children. He was relieved and angry. He shouted at them.

"Hey, you silly kids! What are you doing? You could have been hurt! You should yield when you see a car!"

Mia and Leo stopped and looked at the driver. They were scared and sorry. They realized they had been silly. They had forgotten to be careful and to share. They let go of the ball of yarn. It rolled away and was lost.

They hugged each other and said sorry. They said sorry to the driver too. He forgave them and told them to be more careful. He drove away and left them alone.

Mia and Leo went back to their house. They did not have the ball of yarn anymore. But they still had their cat and snake. They decided to play with them instead. They also decided to be more careful and to share. They learned their lesson from the ball of yarn.

But then, something strange happened. The queen doll's smile turned into a frown. Her crown fell off and her dress ripped. She looked at Lily with angry eyes and said, "I am not your doll. I am a fake queen. I came here to trick you and eat your cookies and juice. Now I will eat you too!" She opened her mouth and tried to bite Lily.

She also learned that being kind and forgiving is better than being angry and mean. She was happy with her dolls and her mom. She was a good girl and a good queen.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little girl named Clara. She loved to play outside and didn't want to do her chores. Today her mother asked her to go and clean up the living room. "Let's delay it for a little bit," said Clara.

But her mother answered firmly: "No, we can't delay it. This needs to be done today."

Clara accepted her mother's answer and decided to get to work. Since she was a bit tired from running around all day, she brought a spoon and a cup of warm milk with her. She used the spoon to clean up the living room, making sure to get into all of the tight corners. As she worked, she thought to herself, "This isn't so bad after all. Delaying always takes longer than if I'd just do it right away."

When she was done, Clara was proud of her work. She finished almost as quickly as she would have if she'd start right away.

The moral of this story is that when you procrastinate, it often takes longer to finish a task than it would have had you started it from the beginning. Just like Clara found out, it's best to leave delaying for later and just do the work right away.

Bob liked to explore when he took a walk in the park. One day he noticed a small wet volcano on the ground. He squatted down to take a closer look.

"What is this?" thought Bob.

Just then, a voice behind him said, "It's a volcano, little one."

Bob looked up and saw a kind old man. 

"My, my," continued the old man, "It looks like this volcano is shrinking! I've seen this before. It happens when the volcano is wet." 

Bob was curious. He asked the old man what he meant.

The old man smiled and explained that when a volcano is wet, its size will shrink, and the wetness will help make it small.

Bob was amazed. He thanked the old man, and continued his exploration.

One day, they saw a new thing in the park. It was a big rope with a loop at the end. It was hanging from a tree. Lily and Tom wondered what it was for.

"Maybe it is for jumping," Lily said.

"Or for flying," Tom said.

They decided to try it. Lily went first. She put her foot in the loop and pulled the rope. She felt the rope lift her up. She felt happy and excited.

"Look at me, Tom! I am flying!" she shouted.

Tom clapped his hands and cheered. He wanted to try it too. He waited for Lily to come down. But Lily did not come down. She was stuck. The loop was too tight around her foot. She could not get it off. She started to cry.

"Help me, Tom! I am stuck!" she cried.

Tom ran to the tree. He tried to pull the rope. But the rope was too high and too strong. He could not reach it. He felt scared and worried.

"Help! Help!" he yelled.

A man heard them. He was walking his dog in the park. He saw Lily and Tom. He saw the rope. He knew what it was for. It was not for playing. It was for catching animals. It was a trap. He felt angry and sorry.

He ran to the tree. He had a knife. He cut the rope. He freed Lily. He lifted her down. He checked her foot. It was red and sore. But it was not broken. He felt relieved and glad.

"Are you okay, little girl?" he asked.

Lily nodded. She hugged him. She thanked him. She felt safe and grateful.

Tom hugged Lily. He hugged the man. He thanked him too. He felt happy and thankful.

The man smiled. He told them to be careful. He told them not to play with the rope. He told them it was dangerous. He told them it was a trap. He felt kind and helpful.

Lily and Tom felt guilty. They knew they did a bad thing. They knew they should not have played with the rope. They knew they could have been hurt. They felt sorry and ashamed.

They said sorry to the man. They said sorry to each other. They said sorry to the animals. They felt sorry and sorry.

They learned a lesson. They learned to be safe. They learned to be smart. They learned to be good. They felt better and better.

Ella and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with a swing, a slide and a sandbox. They also had a dog named Spot who was very friendly and liked to chase balls.

One morning, Ella and Ben woke up very early. They looked out the window and saw the sky was pink and orange. They knew it was sunrise, when the sun comes up and makes the day bright. They wanted to see the sunrise better, so they put on their shoes and ran outside.

They saw the sun peeking over the hills and shining on the flowers and the grass. They felt the warm air and heard the birds singing. They smiled and said, "Wow, the sunrise is so pretty!"

They decided to play on the swing and the slide, and they called Spot to join them. They had a lot of fun, until they heard a loud scream from the house. They stopped and looked at each other, scared. They wondered who was screaming and why.

They ran back to the house and saw their grandma standing on the porch. She was elderly, with white hair and glasses. She looked angry and scared. She pointed at the kitchen and said, "There's a mouse in the kitchen! It ran under the table and scared me! Help me get rid of it!"

Ella and Ben looked at each other and giggled. They thought a mouse was not so scary, but they knew their grandma did not like them. They said, "Don't worry, grandma, we'll help you. Come on, Spot, let's catch the mouse!"

They ran into the kitchen, followed by Spot, who barked and wagged his tail. They looked under the table and saw a small brown mouse with a long tail. It squeaked and ran away, but Spot was faster. He chased the mouse and caught it in his mouth. He brought it back to Ella and Ben, who praised him and petted him.

They showed the mouse to their grandma, who said, "Thank you, Ella and Ben, and thank you, Spot. You are very brave and smart. Now, please take the mouse outside and let it go. I don't want it in my house!"

They nodded and said, "Okay, grandma, we will. But can we have some breakfast first? We are hungry from playing and helping."

Their grandma smiled and said, "Of course, you can. You deserve some pancakes and juice. Come on, let's go to the dining room. And don't forget to wash your hands!"

They washed their hands and went to the dining room, where they ate their pancakes and juice. They told their grandma about the sunrise and how beautiful it was. They asked her if she wanted to see it with them next time. She said, "Maybe, if you wake me up gently and not with a scream!"

They laughed and hugged their grandma. They said, "We love you, grandma, and we love the sunrise. And we love Spot, too. He's a good dog."

They finished their breakfast and went outside again, with Spot. They let the mouse go in the grass, where it ran away. They waved goodbye to the mouse and said, "Have a nice day, mouse. And don't come back to our house!"

They played some more on the swing and the slide, and watched the sun go higher in the sky. They felt happy and proud. They had a good morning.

Lily and Tom were scared and sad. They ran away. They cried. They lost their map and their game. They hated Ben. He was bad. He ruined their fun.

Sara and Tom sip the coffee. They make a face. The coffee is harsh. It hurts their tongues and throats. They do not like it. They spit it out and say, "Yuck! Coffee is bad!"

The man laughs and says, "Coffee is not for everyone. Some people like it, some people don't. Maybe when you are older, you will like it. But for now, why don't you join me for some juice and cookies? They are sweet and yummy."

She held her teddy bear tight and cried. Her mom and dad tried to make her feel better. They said the operation would make her well. They said the doctor was very nice. They said they would be with her all the time.

But Lily did not listen. She did not want to go. She did not want to leave her home and her toys and her friends. She did not want to speak to anyone.

At the hospital, a nurse came to take her to a room. She wore a white dress and a funny hat. She smiled at Lily and said, "Hello, Lily. I'm Nurse Anna. I'm here to help you. You are a very brave and beautiful girl. Do you want to speak to me?"

Lily shook her head. She hid her face in her teddy bear. She did not want to speak to Nurse Anna. She did not want to speak to anyone.

Nurse Anna did not give up. She said, "Lily, I know you are scared. But the operation is not so bad. It will be over soon. And then you will feel much better. You will be able to play and run and laugh again. And you will have a special bandage on your arm. Do you want to see it?"

Lily said, "Yes, please."

Nurse Anna helped Lily put the sticker on the bandage. She said, "There. Now you have a beautiful bandage. And you know what? You can have more stickers after the operation. You can decorate your bandage as much as you want. How does that sound?"

Lily smiled. She liked the idea of having more stickers. She liked the idea of having a beautiful bandage. She felt a little less scared. She said, "Thank you, Nurse Anna. You are very nice."

Lily said, "Yes, I think so."

Lily said, "I love you too. I'll see you soon."

She hoped it would not hurt too much. She hoped it would make her well. She hoped she would be able to play and run and laugh again.

She hoped she would have a beautiful bandage.

She liked to smell the sweet aroma of the cake as it baked. But most of all, she liked to taste the cake when it was done.

One day, Anna decided to bake a cake by herself. She wanted to surprise her mom and dad. She remembered the ingredients and the steps, but she did not measure them carefully. She put too much sugar, too little butter, and forgot the eggs. She also added some salt, pepper, and ketchup, because she thought they would make the cake more colorful and spicy.

When the cake was ready, Anna took it out of the oven and put it on a plate. She was very proud of her work. She called her mom and dad to the kitchen and said, "Look, I made a cake for you! Do you want to taste it?"

Her mom and dad smiled and thanked her for her effort. They each took a small bite of the cake and tried not to make a face. The cake was very sweet, very dry, and very weird. They did not like it at all, but they did not want to hurt Anna's feelings.

They said, "Wow, Anna, this is a very...interesting cake. You are very creative and brave to try new things. But you know, sometimes it is better to follow a recipe and measure the ingredients. That way, the cake will be more delicious and more balanced. Do you want to learn how to bake a cake with us next time?"

Anna nodded and said, "Yes, please. I want to learn how to bake a cake like you. I'm sorry, I did not mean to make a bad cake. I just wanted to make you happy."

Her mom and dad hugged her and said, "We are happy, Anna, because you are our daughter and we love you. You are very intelligent and kind, and we are proud of you. But remember, not everything that looks good tastes good. And not everyone who tastes your cake will be as nice as us. Some people might be mean and judge you. Anna said, "Okay, mom and dad. I love you too. And I love cake. Can we bake a cake together now?"

Anna loved to play in the garden with her friends, the birds. She liked to feed them seeds and watch them fly and sing. One day, she saw a new bird in the garden. It was white and soft and had a long tail. Anna thought it was very pretty and wanted to make friends with it.

"Hello, bird," she said. "What is your name?"

The bird looked at her and cooed. Anna smiled and said, "You sound like a dove. Are you a dove?"

The bird nodded and flew closer to Anna. Anna reached out her hand and the bird landed on it. Anna felt its delicate feathers and gentle beak. She was very happy and said, "You are a dove. And you are my friend."

The dove cooed again and rubbed its head against Anna's cheek. Anna giggled and said, "You are very sweet. Do you want some seeds?"

The dove nodded and Anna took some seeds from her pocket. She held them in her palm and the dove pecked them. Anna watched the dove eat and said, "You must be hungry. Where did you come from?"

The dove looked up and pointed with its wing. Anna followed its gaze and saw a big cage in the neighbor's yard. The cage had a sign that said, "For sale. White dove. Very rare and expensive."

Anna gasped and said, "You came from the cage? You escaped?"

The dove nodded and looked sad. Anna felt sorry for the dove and said, "You don't belong in a cage. You belong in the sky. You are free."

The dove smiled and cooed. Anna smiled and said, "You are free. And you are my friend. But you have to be careful. The neighbor might look for you. He might want you back."

The dove nodded and looked around. Anna said, "Don't worry. I will help you. I will hide you in my house. Come with me."

The dove agreed and flew after Anna. Anna ran to her house and opened the door. She said, "Come in, dove. This is your new home."

The dove entered and looked around. Anna said, "This is my room. You can stay here. I have a bed for you and a window for you. You can see the garden and the sky. You can be happy."

The dove cooed and flew to the window. It saw the garden and the sky and felt happy. It flew back to Anna and said, "Thank you, Anna. You are very kind. You are my friend."

Anna hugged the dove and said, "You are welcome, dove. You are very brave. You are my friend."

They smiled and cuddled. They were happy. They were friends.

One sunny day, Basketball and Fake had a quarrel. They were playing a game, and Basketball thought Fake was not playing fair. Basketball was sad and angry. Fake was also sad and angry. They stopped playing and went to different places in the park.

After some time, Basketball and Fake thought about their quarrel. They both felt bad and missed playing together. Basketball decided to find Fake and say sorry. When Basketball found Fake, they both said sorry to each other. They promised to play fair and be good friends again.

From that day on, Basketball and Fake played happily together. They learned that even good friends can have quarrels, but saying sorry and forgiving each other is important. And they all lived happily ever after.

Days went by, and Lily had to wear her other shoes. They were not the same as her special shoe, and she didn't like them as much. She still missed her special shoe and wished she could find it.

One day, while walking to the park, Lily saw her special shoe in the middle of the street. She ran to get it, but a car came and hit her. She was hurt very badly, and her special shoe was ruined. Lily never got to wear her special shoe again, and she missed it every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to play outside all day long. One day, a big storm came and Benny got scared. He looked for a shelter to hide in. He saw an orange house and went inside. 

Inside the shelter, Benny felt safe and warm. He decided to stay there forever. He quit playing outside and stayed inside the orange house every day. He forgot about his friends and family. 

One day, Benny realized that he was lonely and missed his family. He tried to go back outside, but he was too scared. He realized that he made a mistake by quitting playing outside. 

The moral of the story is that it's important to face our fears and not give up on things we love. Benny learned that he needed to be brave and go back outside to be happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a big, big bear. The big bear loved to sleep in the forest. He would sleep all day long. The big bear was very happy when he slept. 

One day, while the big bear was sleeping, a little fox came into the forest. The little fox saw the big bear sleeping and thought it was funny. The little fox started to play tricks on the big bear. The big bear did not like this. The big bear felt a threat from the little fox. 

The big bear woke up and saw the little fox. The big bear roared and scared the little fox away. The little fox ran away and never came back. The big bear went back to sleep, happy and safe. And from that day on, the big bear could sleep without any threats.

One day, a little bird named Tim was flying in the sky. Tim saw a big tree with a hole in it. He thought it would be a perfect home for him. But first, he needed to know if the hole was big enough for him. So, Tim decided to measure the hole with his beak.

Tim flew to the tree and put his open beak near the hole. He said, "I will measure the hole with my mouth." He moved his mouth up and down, left and right. Tim was happy because the hole was just the right size for him. He knew he would fit in the hole.

The next day, Tim invited his friend, Sam the squirrel, over to see his new home. Sam looked at the hole and said, "Wow, you measured it well, Tim! It's a perfect fit for you!" Tim smiled and said, "Yes, I used my open mouth to measure it." They both laughed and played in the tree all day. And from that day on, Tim and Sam became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty boy named Tim. He loved to play hockey with his friends. One day, he found a big hockey stick in the park. Tim was very happy and wanted to play with it.

Tim asked his friend, Sam, "Do you want to play hockey with me?" Sam said, "Yes, but we must return the hockey stick if we find the owner." Tim and Sam played and had lots of fun. But Tim did not want to return the hockey stick.

Later, an old man came to the park. He was very sad. He said, "I lost my hockey stick. Did you see it?" Tim hid the hockey stick and said, "No, I did not see it." The old man walked away, still sad.

Sam was mad at Tim. He said, "You are naughty! We should return the hockey stick to the old man." But Tim did not listen. He kept the hockey stick and played with it all day. The old man never found his hockey stick and stayed sad. Tim's friends did not want to play with him anymore because he was naughty.

Once upon a time, there was a big mountain. A little boy named Tom wanted to go up the mountain. But the mountain was very hard to climb. Tom knew he had to struggle to reach the top.

One day, Tom met a girl named Lily. She wanted to go up the mountain too. Tom said, "Let's go up the mountain together!" Lily said, "Yes! We can help each other!" They started to climb the mountain. They struggled, but they did not give up.

As they climbed, they saw a dead tree. The tree was in their way. Tom and Lily had to find a way to get past the tree. They pushed and pulled, and finally, they moved the tree. They kept climbing the mountain. At last, they reached the top. Tom and Lily were happy. They had struggled, but they made it to the top together.

Once upon a time, there was a big ostrich named Ollie. Ollie loved to paint. One day, he found some bright colors to play with. He was so happy!

Ollie went to his friend, the little bird named Billy. "Look at my bright colors!" said Ollie. "Let's paint together!" Billy was excited too. They started to paint the trees and the grass with the bright colors.

But then, Ollie got an idea. "Let's paint the sun!" he said. Billy thought it was a bad idea, but Ollie didn't listen. He took the bright colors and painted the sun.

Suddenly, the sun was not happy. It got too hot, and the bright colors started to melt. The trees, the grass, and even Ollie and Billy were all covered in the melted colors.

And that is why you should never paint the sun. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man named Tom. Tom had a mask that he loved to wear. One day, he lost his mask and was very sad.

Tom looked for his mask everywhere. He looked under his bed and in the toy box, but he could not find it. Then, he saw the mask high up on a shelf. Tom tried to reach for it, but he was not tall enough.

One day, a small fish named Fin was swimming in the ocean. The water was icy, but Fin liked it. He saw a big rock near the shore and wanted to rest on it. Fin swam closer to the rock, but the tide was very strong. It was hard for him to swim.

As Fin tried to swim to the rock, he met a crab named Carl. Carl said, "Be careful, Fin! The tide can make you soak if you go too close to the shore." Fin was scared, but he really wanted to rest on the rock.

Fin asked Carl for help. Carl thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea! Hold onto my shell, and I will walk to the rock. That way, you won't soak." Fin held onto Carl's shell, and they slowly moved towards the rock.

The tide was strong, but Carl was stronger. They finally reached the rock, and Fin was so happy. He thanked Carl for helping him. They both rested on the rock, enjoying the icy water and the sound of the tide. From that day on, Fin and Carl became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby dog named Bobo. Bobo loved to play with his ball all day long. One day, he saw a shiny watch on the ground. Bobo picked it up with his mouth and ran to show his friend, Kitty.

"Look, Kitty!" said Bobo, as he dropped the watch in front of her. "I found a shiny thing!" Kitty looked at the watch and said, "Oh no, Bobo! This is not a toy. We must find the person who lost it."

Bobo and Kitty walked around, asking their friends if they lost a watch. But no one knew whose watch it was. They were very tired and sad. They wanted to find the owner, but they did not know what to do.

As they walked, they saw a big pond. Bobo had an idea. "Maybe if we drop the watch in the pond, the person who lost it will find it there," he said. Kitty thought it was a good idea, too. So, they dropped the watch in the pond.

But the watch did not float. It sank to the bottom of the pond. Bobo and Kitty felt bad. They could not find the owner, and now the watch was gone forever. They went home, sad that their adventure had a bad ending.

"Wait here, Lily. I have a plan!" Ben says, running to his mom's room.

"Really? You can do that?" Lily asks, surprised and hopeful.

He puts the thread through the needle's eye. He holds the cloth and the doll's dress together. He makes a stitch by pushing the needle in and out of the cloth. He does it again and again until the hole is closed.

"See, Lily? I made a stitch. The hole is gone. Your doll's dress is fixed!" Ben says, holding up the doll.

Lily looks at the doll. She sees the stitch. It is light and neat. She is amazed and happy.

Anna and Ben were twins who lived in a big house with their wealthy parents. They had many toys and clothes and books, but they were not happy. They wanted to go outside and play with other children, but their parents said it was too cold and foggy.

One day, they saw a big hole in the fence that surrounded their house. They decided to sneak out and explore the world. They put on their coats and hats and ran through the hole. They saw a park with swings and slides and a pond. They also saw many children laughing and running and playing.

"Hello, can we play with you?" Anna asked a girl with curly hair and a red dress.

"Sure, what's your name?" the girl said.

"I'm Anna and this is my brother Ben. We live in that big house over there," Anna said, pointing to their house.

"Wow, you must be very wealthy," the girl said. "I'm Lily and I live in that small house over there," she said, pointing to a house that looked old and worn.

"Wealthy? What does that mean?" Ben asked.

"It means you have a lot of money and things," Lily said.

"Oh, we don't care about money and things. We just want to have fun and make friends," Ben said.

"Then you are very lucky," Lily said. "Come on, let's play!"

Anna and Ben had a lot of fun with Lily and the other children. They swung on the swings, slid on the slides, and fed the ducks in the pond. They forgot about the time and the cold and the fog.

But soon, the mist became thicker and darker. They could not see their house or Lily's house anymore. They could only see each other and the park.

"We should go back," Anna said. "Our parents will be worried."

"OK, let's go," Ben said.

They said goodbye to Lily and the other children and thanked them for playing with them. They ran back to the hole in the fence, but they could not find it. The mist was too thick. They were lost.

They started to cry and call for help. They wished they had never left their house. They wished they had listened to their parents.

Then, they heard a familiar voice.

"Anna! Ben! Where are you?" their father shouted.

"Daddy! Daddy! We're here!" Anna and Ben shouted back.

Their father found them and hugged them. He was angry and relieved. He took them back to their house and scolded them for running away. He also told them he loved them and was glad they were safe.

Anna and Ben felt sorry and happy. They said they were sorry and they loved him too. They also told him about Lily and the other children and the park. They asked him if they could play with them again.

Their father smiled and said, "Maybe, but only if you ask me first and if the weather is clear. No more mist adventures, OK?"

"OK, Daddy," Anna and Ben said.

They learned their lesson and never ran away again. They also made friends with Lily and the other children and played with them often. They realized that being wealthy was not as important as being happy and having fun. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to wander around the forest and play with his friends. One day, Benny's family decided to go on a trip to a faraway land. Benny was excited to go on an adventure!

When they arrived at the airport, Benny's mom gave him his passport. "This is your passport, Benny. You need it to go on the plane," she said. Benny was proud of his passport and held onto it tightly.

As they waited for their flight, Benny saw a little girl sitting nearby. She was crying and looked sad. Benny hopped over to her and asked, "Why are you sad?" The little girl replied, "I lost my teddy bear. He's my best friend." Benny felt sorry for her and said, "Don't worry, I'll help you find him. Let's wander around the airport together."

They searched high and low, but couldn't find the teddy bear. Just when they were about to give up, Benny spotted the teddy bear on a bench. "Look, I found your teddy bear!" he exclaimed. The little girl was overjoyed and gave Benny a big hug.

Benny felt happy that he could help someone in need. As they boarded the plane, Benny's mom said, "You're such a good bunny, Benny. I'm proud of you." Benny smiled and held onto his passport, ready for more adventures in the future.

Anna and Ben nod. They like soup. They sit on their chairs and wait for their mom to serve them. Their mom gives them each a bowl of soup and a spoon. She says, "Be careful, the soup is hot. Blow on it before you eat."

Anna and Ben blow on their soup. They taste it. It is yummy. They say, "Thank you, mom. This is a good dinner." Their mom smiles. She says, "You are welcome, my loves. I am glad you like it."

After they finish their soup, their mom gives them a cookie for dessert. They eat their cookie and drink some milk. They say, "We are full, mom. Can we play with our cars again?" Their mom says, "Yes, you can. But first, wash your hands and put your dishes in the sink." Anna and Ben do as they are told. Then they run back to their room and play with their cars until bedtime. They have fun driving their cars and making sounds. They are happy.

Lila was a little girl who liked to ride in her dad's big car. She felt safe and happy when she sat in her seat and heard the buckle click. Her dad was a wealthy man who worked hard and bought nice things for Lila and her mom.

One day, her dad said they were going to visit a new friend. He said the friend was very kind and generous and had a big house with a lot of toys. Lila was excited and curious. She wondered what the friend looked like and what toys he had.

They drove for a long time and reached a big gate. Her dad pressed a button and the gate opened. They drove up a long driveway and saw a huge house with many windows and a fountain. Lila gasped. She had never seen such a big house before.

They parked the car and got out. Her dad held her hand and walked to the door. He rang the bell and waited. Lila heard a loud bark and saw a big dog run to the door. She felt scared and hid behind her dad. The dog looked angry and fierce.

The door opened and a man came out. He smiled and said, "Welcome, welcome, my friends! I'm so glad you're here!" He bent down and petted the dog. He said, "Don't worry, this is Rufus. He's very friendly and loves children. He just wants to say hello."

He picked up Lila and hugged her. He said, "You must be Lila. You're so pretty and sweet. I have a surprise for you. Come, let me show you." He carried her inside and showed her a big room full of toys. There were dolls, cars, books, puzzles, and more. Lila felt happy and amazed. She said, "Wow, thank you, thank you! You're so nice!"

The man said, "You're very welcome, Lila. I'm your grandpa. I've been looking for you and your dad for a long time. I'm so happy to finally meet you. You're my family and I love you very much." He kissed her cheek and hugged her again.

Lila smiled and hugged him back. She said, "I love you too, grandpa. You're my family too. Can I play with Rufus and the toys?"

Grandpa said, "Of course, you can. You can play with anything you want. This is your home too, Lila. You're always welcome here." He put her down and watched her run to Rufus and the toys. He felt a tear in his eye and thanked his son for bringing Lila to him. He said, "This is the best day of my life."

Tim and Lily were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big slide that looked very fun. Tim wanted to go on the slide, but Lily was scared. She said, "No, Tim, the slide is too high and too fast. I want to stay on the swings."

Tim said, "Don't be silly, Lily. The slide is not scary. It is fun. Come with me. I will hold your hand."

Lily shook her head. She said, "No, Tim, I don't want to. You go. I will remain on the swings."

Tim was angry. He said, "Fine, Lily. You are a baby. I will go on the slide by myself. You will miss the fun."

Tim ran to the slide and climbed up the ladder. He looked down and saw how high and steep the slide was. He felt a little scared, but he did not want to show it. He said to himself, "I am brave. I can do this."

He pushed himself off the ladder and slid down the slide. He went very fast and felt the wind in his hair. He was having fun, until he saw a big rock at the end of the slide. He tried to stop, but he could not. He hit the rock with a loud thud and fell off the slide. He hurt his knee and his elbow and his head. He cried out loud.

Lily heard Tim's cry and looked up. She saw him lying on the ground, bleeding and crying. She felt sorry for him. She ran to him and hugged him. She said, "Tim, are you okay? I'm sorry you got hurt. I love you."

Tim hugged her back. He said, "Lily, I'm sorry I was mean to you. You were right. The slide was too high and too fast. I love you too."

They both learned a lesson that day. They learned to respect each other's will and feelings. They also learned to be careful and slow when they play. They went home with their mom and dad, who gave them hugs and kisses and band-aids. They were happy and safe.

Sara and Tom liked to play in the woods behind their house. They liked to find pine cones and make houses for their toys. One day, they saw a big pine tree with a hole in it. They wondered what was inside.

"Can we look in the hole?" Sara asked Tom.

"Maybe. But be careful. There might be something scary in there," Tom said.

They walked closer to the pine tree and peeked in the hole. It was dark and empty. They saw nothing but dirt and leaves.

"Can we go in?" Sara asked again.

"I don't know. It looks too small for us," Tom said.

But Sara was curious. She crawled into the hole and said, "Come on, Tom. It's not scary. It's fun."

Tom followed her, but he felt nervous. He wished they had brought a flashlight. He hoped they would not get lost.

They crawled deeper into the hole, until they saw a faint light at the end. They reached the light and saw another hole. They looked out and saw a different part of the woods. They saw a pond and a bridge and some ducks.

"Wow, this is cool," Sara said. "We found a secret tunnel."

"Maybe we should go back," Tom said. "Mom and Dad might be looking for us."

But Sara wanted to explore more. She said, "Let's go see the ducks. Maybe they have babies."

She crawled out of the hole and ran to the pond. Tom followed her, but he felt more nervous. He wondered if they could find their way back.

They reached the pond and saw the ducks. They were cute and fluffy. Sara and Tom smiled and tried to feed them some bread. But then they heard a loud quack and saw a big duck with a red head. It was angry and chased them away.

"Run, Tom, run!" Sara shouted.

They ran back to the hole, but they saw something else. They saw a big bear with a black fur. It was hungry and smelled them. It roared and followed them.

"Help, Sara, help!" Tom cried.

They ran faster and faster, until they reached the hole. They crawled in and hoped the bear would not fit. They heard it scratch and growl and try to get in. They were scared and cried.

They crawled back to the other hole, where they had come from. They hoped to see their house and their parents. But they saw something else. They saw a big fire with a red flame. It was burning the woods and the pine tree. It crackled and smoked and reached the hole. They felt the heat and the pain.

They screamed and screamed, until they woke up. They were in their beds, in their room, in their house. They were safe and sound. It was all a dream.

They hugged each other and said, "I'm sorry, Sara. I'm sorry, Tom."

They heard their mom and dad come in. They asked them what was wrong. They told them about their dream. They said they were sorry for being naughty and going into the hole.

Their mom and dad hugged them and said, "It's okay, Sara. It's okay, Tom. We're glad you're okay. We love you."

They said they loved them too. They said they would never go into the hole again. They said they would always listen to their mom and dad.

They went back to sleep, and dreamed of happy things.
