She waited until the show was over and then ran to the stage. She saw the dancer she liked and called her name. The dancer turned around and saw Lily.

"Hi, I'm Lily. You are so good at dancing. Are you my sister or cousin?" Lily asked.

You are not my sister or cousin. You are nothing. You will never be a dancer like me. You are just a silly girl with a stupid dream."

Lily felt a sharp pain in her chest. She fell to the ground and dropped her teddy bear. She started to cry. She did not understand why the dancer was so mean to her. She did not do anything wrong. She just wanted to be her friend and learn from her.

Her mom heard her cry and ran to her. She hugged her and tried to comfort her. She saw the dancer walking away and glared at her. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. She is not a good dancer. She is a bad person. She does not know how to be kind and respectful. She does not deserve your admiration. You have a wonderful dream and you can achieve it. You are a cheerful and talented girl. You just need to work hard and practice. And you will always have me and dad to support you and love you."

Lily looked at her mom and smiled. She wiped her tears and hugged her back. She said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. You are the best mom in the world. You are right. I will not give up on my dream. I will be a better dancer than her. And I will be a good person too."

You learned that you should not judge people by their appearance. You learned that you should always be polite and respectful to others. And you learned that you should follow your dream and be yourself. I'm proud of you, Lily. You are my little star."

Lily smiled and thanked her dad. She felt better and happier. She went to her room and danced with her teddy bear. She dreamed of becoming a dancer and making people smile. She did not think of the mean dancer anymore. She thought of her mom and dad and her friends. She thought of the good things in life. She was a cheerful girl with a big dream. And she was happy.

Lily looked at the penguin. It was black and white and had a beak and wings. It was very different from the giraffe. She tried to say the word "penguin" but it was hard.

"Pen...pen...ping?" she said.

"Almost, Lily," her mom said. "It is penguin. Try again."

Lily repeated the word. "Penguin. Penguin. Penguin."

"Good job, Lily!" her mom said. "You are learning new words every day. You are a brilliant reader."

Lily smiled. She felt happy and proud. She hugged her mom and her book. She wanted to read more and more. She loved words.

Tom and Anna were twins. They liked to play together, but sometimes they fought. One day, they had a big fight over a toy. Tom wanted to play with the toy, but Anna said it was hers. They pulled and pushed and shouted.

"Give me the toy, it's mine!" Tom said.

"No, it's mine, you had it yesterday!" Anna said.

They were so angry that they did not hear their mom calling them for lunch. They did not see their dad coming into the room. They did not notice the toy breaking in their hands.

"Stop it, you two!" their dad said. "Look what you have done! You broke the toy, and you made a mess. You are both foolish. Go to your rooms and think about what you did."

Tom and Anna felt sad and sorry. They dropped the toy and ran to their rooms. They did not want to eat lunch. They did not want to play anymore. They wanted to say sorry to each other and to their mom and dad.

Tom lay on his bed and thought. He wished he had not fought with Anna. He wished he had shared the toy. He wished he had listened to his mom. He closed his eyes and prayed.

"Dear God, please help me to be a good brother. Please help me to be kind and fair. Please help me to say sorry to Anna and to mom and dad. Please fix the toy and make it new again. Amen."

Anna sat on her chair and thought. She wished she had not fought with Tom. She wished she had let him play with the toy. She wished she had heard her dad. She opened her mouth and prayed.

"Dear God, please help me to be a good sister. Please help me to be gentle and nice. Please help me to say sorry to Tom and to mom and dad. Please mend the toy and make it whole again. Amen."

Then, Tom and Anna heard a knock on their doors. It was their mom. She smiled and said, "I have a surprise for you. Come with me."

She took them to the bathroom. There, on the sink, was a new toy. It was the same as the one they had broken, but better. It had bright colors and shiny buttons. It made funny sounds and lights.

"Wow!" Tom and Anna said.

"This is for you," their mom said. "Your dad and I bought it for you. We know you love this toy, and we love you. We are sorry we were angry with you. We know you are sorry too. Can you forgive us?"

Tom and Anna hugged their mom and said, "Yes, we forgive you. We love you too. And we are sorry we were foolish. Can you forgive us?"

Their mom nodded and said, "Of course, we forgive you. You are our children, and we are proud of you. Now, why don't you play with your new toy together, and then we can have lunch?"

Tom and Anna smiled and said, "Yes, let's do that. Thank you, mom. Thank you, dad. Thank you, God."

They took the new toy and went to their room. They played with it happily, and they shared it nicely. They did not fight anymore. They were good twins.

Lily came home from school. She was thirsty and wanted to drink from her mug. She looked for it on the table, but it was not there. She asked her mom, but she did not know. She asked Tommy, but he did not answer. She went to his room and opened the door.

She saw Tommy with the scissors and the mug. He had cut the princess and stuck it on the wall. He had also cut the handle and the rim of the mug. The mug was broken and ruined. Lily was very angry and sad. She screamed at Tommy and grabbed the scissors from him.

"Tommy, you are a bad boy! You cut my mug! You spoiled my mug! How could you do this to me?" she yelled.

Tommy was scared and sorry. He did not mean to make Lily angry and sad. He just wanted to make his art better. He did not know Lily loved her mug so much. He tried to say sorry, but Lily did not listen. She ran to her mom and told her what Tommy did. Mom came to Tommy's room and saw the mess. She was not happy. She took Tommy to the corner and made him sit there. She said he had to stay there until he learned his lesson. Tommy felt very bad. He wished he had not cut Lily's mug. He wished he had not spoiled her mug. He wished he had not made her angry and sad. He wished he had been a good boy.

"Look, Lily, I found a shiny watch!" Tim said, holding up a silver watch he saw on the grass. "Maybe someone lost it. Can I examine it with the magnifying glass?"

"Sure, Tim, but be careful. It might be someone's special watch. Maybe they will come back for it." Lily said, handing him the magnifying glass. She looked around to see if anyone was looking for the watch.

Tim looked at the watch with the magnifying glass. He saw the numbers, the hands and the buttons. He pressed one of the buttons and the watch made a beep sound. He pressed another button and the watch showed a different time.

"Wow, this is not a regular watch. It can do many things. Maybe it is a magic watch." Tim said, amazed.

"Or maybe it is a spy watch. Maybe someone is using it to spy on us." Lily said, a little scared.

Just then, a man came running towards them. He was wearing a suit and sunglasses. He looked very serious.

"Hey, kids, have you seen my watch? I dropped it here when I was chasing a bad guy. It is very important. It has a secret message on it." He said, panting.

Tim and Lily looked at each other. They did not know what to do. They did not want to give the man the watch, but they did not want to keep it either.

"Um, is this your watch?" Tim asked, holding up the watch.

"Yes, yes, that's it. Thank you, kids. You saved the day. You are very smart and brave." The man said, taking the watch from Tim. He smiled and winked at them.

"Who are you?" Lily asked, curious.

"I'm a secret agent. I work for the good guys. And this watch is a special gadget. It can do many things, like tell the time, send messages and make noises. But it is not a toy. It is very dangerous. You should not play with it." The man said, putting the watch on his wrist.

"Wow, a secret agent. That's cool. Can we be secret agents too?" Tim asked, excited.

"Maybe when you grow up. But for now, you should just be kids. And kids should play with regular things, like balls, dolls and books. And if you ever find something that is not yours, you should give it back or ask for help. OK?" The man said, patting their heads.

"OK." Tim and Lily said, nodding.

"Good. Now, I have to go. The bad guy is still out there. But don't worry, I'll catch him. Bye, kids." The man said, running away.

"Bye, secret agent." Tim and Lily said, waving.

They watched him go. They felt a little sad, but also a little proud. They had met a secret agent and examined a spy watch. That was not a regular day. That was an adventure.

One night, a little boy named Tom looked out of his window and saw many stars in the sky. He wondered what they were and how they tasted. He asked his mom, "Mom, can I eat a star?"

His mom smiled and said, "No, Tom, you can't eat a star. Stars are very far away and very hot. They are not food for us. They are lights that shine at night."

"But why do they shine?" Tom asked.

"Because they are made of fire and gas," his mom said. "They are like big balls of fire that burn and glow. They are very beautiful, but also very dangerous. If you try to eat a star, you will get burned and hurt."

Tom felt scared and curious. He wanted to see a star up close, but he also did not want to get burned. He asked his mom, "How can I see a star, then?"

His mom hugged him and said, "You can see a star with a telescope. A telescope is a tool that makes things look bigger and closer. Maybe someday we can get a telescope and see the stars together. But for now, you can see them with your eyes and make a wish."

Tom liked that idea. He looked at the stars again and picked one that was bright and shiny. He closed his eyes and made a wish. He wished that he could have a telescope and see the stars with his mom. He also wished that he could have a cookie and some milk before bed. He opened his eyes and said, "Mom, I made a wish. Can I have a cookie and some milk, please?"

His mom laughed and said, "Sure, Tom, you can have a cookie and some milk. But only one, okay? You don't want to eat too much before bed. Come on, let's go to the kitchen."

Tom followed his mom to the kitchen. He was happy and sleepy. He ate his cookie and drank his milk. He thanked his mom and gave her a kiss. He said, "Mom, I love you. And I love the stars. But I don't want to eat them. They are too hot and bad."

His mom said, "I love you too, Tom. And I'm glad you don't want to eat the stars. They are not for us. They are for the sky. Now, let's go to bed. It's late and you need to sleep."

Tom nodded and yawned. He went to his room with his mom. He got into his bed and snuggled with his teddy bear. He looked out of his window and saw the stars again. He smiled and said, "Good night, stars. Thank you for shining. Maybe someday I will see you with a telescope. But for now, I will dream of you."

He closed his eyes and fell asleep. He dreamed of stars and cookies and his mom. He was happy and warm. He did not eat a star, but he felt like one.

"Wow, that was a wild bear!" Ben said.

"I'm glad we are safe. But I'm sad we lost our pears." Mia said.

"Maybe we can get some more tomorrow. But we have to be more careful and watch out for bears." Ben said.

They hugged each other and went to find their mom. They told her what happened and she gave them some cookies and milk. They learned a lesson that day: never load your wagon with pears near a wild bear.

"Hi, I'm Fred," said the wet frog. "Do you like to play in the puddles too?"

"No, I don't like to get wet," said Harry, shaking his big horn. "I like to stay dry in the sun."

Fred thought for a moment and then smiled. "I have an idea! Let's play a game. You can stay dry in the sun, and I will jump in the puddles. When I am wet, I will try to make you wet too by shaking the water off me."

Harry laughed and agreed to play the game. They played all day long. Fred would jump in the puddles and try to make Harry wet, but Harry would use his big horn to block the water. They laughed and had so much fun together.

At the end of the day, Fred and Harry were both tired but happy. They had made a new friend and found a fun game to play together. From that day on, they played together in the forest, with Fred always trying to make Harry wet and Harry always trying to stay dry.

She felt something slip under her foot and she lost her balance. She fell down again and hit her head on the cabinet. She cried out loud and felt a bump on her forehead.

Mommy heard her cry and ran to her room. She saw Jenny on the floor, holding her head and her knee. She picked her up and hugged her.

"Oh, Jenny, what happened? Are you okay?" Mommy asked.

"I wanted to play, but I fell down and hurt myself again," Jenny sobbed.

Mommy kissed her head and her knee and said, "I'm sorry, honey. You need to be careful and stay in bed. You have two boo-boos now. But don't worry, they will heal soon. I love you very much."

She carried Jenny back to her bed and tucked her in. She gave her a teddy bear and a glass of water. She turned on the lamp and said, "How about I read you a story? Would you like that?"

Jenny nodded and smiled a little. She liked stories. She snuggled with her teddy bear and listened to Mommy's voice. She felt warm and safe. She forgot about her pain and her gloom. She closed her eyes and fell asleep.

Tim and Lily were adventurous kids. They liked to explore new places and try new things. One day, they found a big board near the river. It was long and wide and flat.

"Let's play with the board!" Tim said. "We can use it as a boat and sail on the water."

Lily was not sure. She looked at the river. It was fast and deep and noisy. She was scared of the water.

"I don't know, Tim," she said. "The water looks dangerous. Maybe we should not play with the board."

But Tim did not listen. He was too excited. He dragged the board to the edge of the river and jumped on it. He called to Lily.

"Come on, Lily, don't be afraid. It's fun. Trust me!"

Lily did not want to disappoint Tim. She wanted to be adventurous too. She trusted Tim. She stepped on the board with him. But as soon as she did, the board slipped and floated away. Tim and Lily screamed. They had no control over the board. It was moving too fast. They saw rocks and branches and rapids ahead. They were in trouble.

Luckily, a fisherman saw them. He was in a real boat with a paddle. He quickly rowed to them and helped them get off the board. He brought them to the shore and checked if they were okay. They were wet and cold and scared, but not hurt.

The fisherman was angry. He scolded Tim and Lily.

"What were you thinking, kids? That board is not a boat. It's not safe. You could have drowned or hit something. You should never play with things you don't know near the water. You should always be careful and listen to your friends who are afraid. They might be right."

Tim and Lily felt ashamed. They realized they had been foolish and reckless. They apologized to the fisherman and thanked him for saving them. They learned a lesson. They learned that being adventurous is good, but being smart and safe is better. They learned that trust is important, but so is caution. They learned that sometimes, fear is a friend, not an enemy.

The man was ignorant. He did not listen to Sam. He said, "You are a silly boy. You do not need a goat. You can buy many things with ten coins. Give me your goat now or I will take him by force."

The man tried to grab Sam's goat by the rope. But Sam's goat was not afraid. He used his horns and pushed the man away. The man fell down and hurt his nose. He ran away, crying and bleeding.

Sam hugged his goat and said, "You are a brave goat. I am proud of you. You are my goat. I own you. You are my friend. I love you."

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park with their mom and dad. One day, they see a big hill in the park. They want to walk to the top and see what is there.

"Can we go, mom? Can we go, dad?" they ask.

"Sure, but be careful. It is a long walk and the hill is steep," mom says.

"OK, we will. Come on, Ben!" Anna says.

They hold hands and start to walk. They see many things on the way: flowers, birds, bugs, rocks. They stop to look at them and talk to them.

"Hello, flower. You are pretty. What is your name?" Anna says.

"Hello, bird. You are fast. Where are you going?" Ben says.

They keep walking and walking. They get tired and thirsty. They see a small stream near the hill. They go to the stream and drink some water. They find a spoon on the ground. They wonder who left it there.

"Maybe someone was having a picnic and forgot it," Anna says.

"Maybe it is a magic spoon and can make wishes come true," Ben says.

They take turns holding the spoon and making wishes. They wish for candy, toys, books, and more.

They hear mom and dad calling them. They look up and see them waving from the bottom of the hill. They are very distant. They wave back and start to walk down.

"Did you have fun, kids?" mom asks.

"Yes, we did. We saw many things and we found a spoon," Anna says.

"A spoon? What did you do with it?" dad asks.

"We made wishes with it. It is a magic spoon," Ben says.

They show mom and dad the spoon. Mom and dad smile and hug them.

"That is a very special spoon. Maybe it will make your wishes come true. But you know what? You already have the best thing you can wish for: each other," mom says.

Anna and Ben nod and hug each other. They are happy. They walk home with mom and dad, holding the spoon and their hands.

"Give me the car, Ben!" Lily said. "It is my turn!"

"No, it is mine!" Ben said. "You have the doll!"

Mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw them fighting over the car. She was not happy.

Lily and Ben looked at Mom with their big eyes. They did not want to be in trouble. They repeated after Mom: "I will share and be nice."

Mom smiled and hugged them. She gave them each a cookie. The cookie was sweet and yummy.

"See, sharing and being nice is better than fighting and being bitter," Mom said. "Now, can you play together nicely?"

Lily loved to spend time with her daddy. He was very busy with his work, so it was rare that they could play together. Sometimes, he would take her to the park, or read her a book, or make her a snack. Lily was always happy when her daddy was home.

One day, Lily saw a big box in the living room. She asked her daddy what was inside. He said it was a surprise for her birthday. Lily was curious and excited. She wanted to see the surprise right away. She asked her daddy if she could open the box. He said no, she had to wait until her birthday.

Lily was sad and angry. She did not want to wait. She wanted to spend time with her daddy and the surprise. She thought he was being mean and unfair. She decided to open the box when he was not looking. She sneaked into the living room and lifted the lid.

Inside the box, there was a beautiful doll. It had long hair, a pretty dress, and shiny shoes. Lily gasped. She loved the doll. She wanted to hug it and play with it. She reached for the doll, but then she heard her daddy's voice.

"Lily, what are you doing?" he asked, sounding upset. He had seen her from the kitchen. He walked into the living room and saw the open box and the doll. He looked at Lily with a sad and angry face. He said, "Lily, you disobeyed me. You spoiled the surprise. You were not supposed to open the box until your birthday. How could you do this?"

Lily felt scared and sorry. She realized she had made a mistake. She had hurt her daddy's feelings. She had ruined the rare and special gift he had bought for her. She started to cry. She said, "I'm sorry, daddy. I was curious and excited. I wanted to see the surprise. I wanted to spend time with you and the doll. I didn't mean to be bad. Please don't be mad at me."

Her daddy sighed. He was disappointed and hurt, but he also loved his daughter. He knew she was young and impulsive. He knew she did not understand the value of the gift and the meaning of the surprise. He decided to forgive her and teach her a lesson. He said, "Lily, I love you, but you have to learn to listen and wait. The surprise was meant to make you happy, not sad. The doll was meant to be a reward, not a punishment. You have to respect my rules and my wishes. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She said, "I understand, daddy. I'm sorry, daddy. I love you, daddy." She hugged him and said, "Thank you for the doll. It's beautiful. Can we still play with it?"

Her daddy smiled. He said, "Yes, we can still play with it. But only after you clean up the mess and apologize to your mommy. And next time, when I say no, you have to say okay. Deal?"

Lily said, "Deal, daddy. Thank you, daddy. You're the best daddy." She kissed him and said, "Happy birthday to me."

Lily liked to draw with pastels. Pastels were soft and colorful. She could make pretty pictures with them. She had many pastels in her box. She had red, yellow, blue, green, pink, purple, and more.

One day, Lily wanted to draw a rainbow. She took out her pastels and a big paper. She started to draw a curve with red. Then she drew another curve with orange. Then she drew another curve with yellow. She was happy with her rainbow.

She showed her rainbow to her mom. "Look, mom, I made a rainbow!" she said.

Mom smiled and said, "That's very nice, Lily. You used all the colors of the rainbow. Can you repeat the colors for me?"

Lily nodded and said, "Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet."

Mom clapped and said, "Very good, Lily. You are very smart. Do you know what indigo and violet are?"

Lily shook her head and said, "No, mom. What are they?"

Mom said, "They are the last two colors of the rainbow. They are like blue and purple, but a little different. Indigo is a dark blue, and violet is a light purple. Do you want to see them?"

Lily said, "Yes, mom. Please show me."

Mom took out two pastels from the box. One was indigo and one was violet. She showed them to Lily and said, "This is indigo, and this is violet. Can you repeat their names?"

Lily looked at the pastels and said, "Indigo, violet."

Mom said, "That's right, Lily. You are very good at repeating. Do you want to try to draw with them?"

Lily said, "Yes, mom. Thank you."

Mom gave Lily the pastels and said, "You're welcome, Lily. Have fun drawing."

Lily took the pastels and started to draw with them. She liked how they looked on the paper. She made flowers and stars and hearts with them. She was happy with her drawing.

She showed her drawing to her mom. "Look, mom, I made more things with indigo and violet!" she said.

Mom looked at the drawing and said, "That's very beautiful, Lily. You are very creative. I love your drawing."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you."

Mom hugged Lily and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are my sweet pastel girl."

Ben is sad and angry. He loves his rocket and he worked hard to make it. He wants to get it back from Fluffy.

"It's okay, Lily," he says, trying to be brave. "Maybe we can fix it. Let's go find Fluffy and get my bottle back."

Ben and Lily get up and follow Fluffy. They see him hiding under the table with the bottle. He is playing with it and making it squeak.

"Fluffy, give me my bottle!" Ben says, reaching for it.

"Meow!" Fluffy says, holding it tighter.

Ben and Lily try to get the bottle from Fluffy, but he is too fast and too strong. He scratches them and runs away again.

"Ow, Fluffy, that hurts!" Lily says, rubbing her arm.

"Bad cat, bad cat!" Ben says, shaking his fist.

They chase Fluffy around the house, but they can't catch him. He is too clever and too clumsy. He knocks over lamps, books, vases and pictures. He makes a big mess.

"Fluffy, stop!" Ben and Lily say, but Fluffy doesn't stop.

Mom and Dad hear the noise and come to see what's going on. They see Ben and Lily running after Fluffy and the mess he made.

"What are you doing, kids?" Mom asks, surprised.

"Fluffy took my rocket and broke it!" Ben says, pointing at the cat.

"Fluffy is a naughty cat!" Lily says, nodding.

Mom and Dad look at Fluffy and see the bottle in his mouth. They understand what happened.

"Oh, Fluffy, you silly cat!" Mom says, shaking her head.

"Fluffy, come here!" Dad says, calling him.

Fluffy sees Mom and Dad and drops the bottle. He runs to them and rubs his head against their legs. He purrs and looks at them with his big eyes.

"Meow!" Fluffy says, as if to say sorry.

Mom and Dad pick up Fluffy and cuddle him. They love Fluffy, even if he is a clumsy cat.

"Fluffy, you can't take Ben's toys and break them," Mom says, gently.

"Fluffy, you have to be careful and not make a mess," Dad says, softly.

Ben and Lily come closer and look at Fluffy. They are still mad at him, but they also love him. He is their cat, after all.

"Fluffy, you are a bad cat, but we forgive you," Ben says, touching his nose.

"Fluffy, you are a silly cat, but we still like you," Lily says, stroking his fur.

Fluffy licks their hands and makes a happy sound.

"Meow!" Fluffy says, as if to say thank you.

Mom and Dad smile and hug Ben and Lily. They are proud of them for being kind and forgiving.

"Kids, you are good kids," Mom says, kissing them.

"Kids, you are sweet kids," Dad says, hugging them.

Ben and Lily smile and hug Mom and Dad. They are happy and grateful.

"Mom, Dad, we love you," Ben and Lily say, together.

They all sit on the couch and cuddle with Fluffy. They forget about the rocket and the mess. They are a happy family.

The end.

Anna and Ben are afraid. They want to go back to their mom and dad. But they are too far. They don't know what to do. They whisper to each other and hope the pirates don't see them.

Suddenly, they hear a loud voice. It is their dad. He is calling their names. He is looking for them. He is angry and worried. He is strong and brave. He sees the pirates and the boat. Anna and Ben are sorry. They hug their dad and say they are sorry. They say they love him too. They say they won't do it again. They say they are glad he is strong and brave. They say they are glad he found them.

They go back to their mom and their sand castle. They tell her what happened. She is shocked and relieved. She hugs them and kisses them. She tells them to be safe and happy. She tells them she loves them.

They play at the beach again. They make a new sand castle. They look for shells. They swim in the water, but not too far. They have fun and laugh. They are happy. They are a family.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the woods near their house. One day, they find a big cave. They want to see what is inside.

"Let's go in," Tim says. He is brave and curious.

"No, it is dark and scary," Sam says. He is careful and afraid.

"Come on, don't be a baby," Tim says. He walks into the cave.

Sam follows him. He does not want to be alone.

They see a lot of bones and fur on the ground. They hear a loud snore. They see a big wolf sleeping in the corner.

"Wow, look at that," Tim says. He wants to touch the wolf.

"Shh, don't wake him up," Sam says. He wants to run away.

But Tim does not listen. He goes closer to the wolf. He reaches out his hand.

The wolf opens his eyes. He sees Tim and Sam. He growls.

Tim and Sam scream. They turn around and run.

But the wolf is faster. He jumps and blocks the exit.

"Please, don't eat us," Tim says. He is sorry and scared.

"Please, be polite," Sam says. He is polite and hopeful.

The wolf looks at them. He thinks for a moment. He says:

"Polite? What does that mean?"

Tim and Sam are surprised. They did not know the wolf can talk.

"It means you are nice and kind and friendly," Sam says.

"Nice and kind and friendly?" the wolf says. "Why should I be that?"

"Because it is good and right and fair," Sam says.

"Good and right and fair?" the wolf says. "How do you know that?"

"Because our mom and dad told us," Sam says.

"Mom and dad?" the wolf says. "What are they?"

"They are our family. They love us and take care of us and teach us things," Sam says.

"Family? Love? Teach?" the wolf says. "I don't have those. I only have myself. I am alone and hungry and angry."

Tim and Sam feel sad for the wolf. They say:

"Maybe you can have those too. Maybe you can be our friend. Maybe we can share our food and play with you and learn from you."

"Friend? Share? Play? Learn?" the wolf says. "What are those?"

"They are fun and happy and good things," Sam says.

"Fun and happy and good?" the wolf says. "I never had those. I only had fear and pain and hate."

Tim and Sam feel sorry for the wolf. They say:

"Maybe you can try those. Maybe you can give them a chance. Maybe you can change your life."

"Change my life?" the wolf says. "How can I do that?"

"By being polite," Sam says.

"By being polite," Tim says.

The wolf thinks for a long time. He looks at Tim and Sam. He sees their eyes and smiles. He feels something new in his heart.

He says:

"Okay. I will try. I will be polite. I will not eat you. I will let you go. I will be your friend."

Tim and Sam are happy. They hug the wolf. They say:

"Thank you. You are polite. You are our friend."

They leave the cave. They take the wolf with them. They go to their house. They introduce the wolf to their mom and dad. They share their food and play with him and learn from him.

The wolf is happy. He has a family. He has love. He has fun. He has changed his life.

He is polite.

"Look, Tom, I can make a hat with wheat!" Lily says. She puts some wheat on her head and smiles.

"That's funny, Lily. I can make a sword with wheat!" Tom says. He holds some wheat like a stick and pretends to fight.

They have fun with the wheat. But they do not see the farmer. The farmer is angry. He works hard to grow the wheat. He does not like children to mess with his wheat.

"Hey, you two, get off my wheat!" the farmer shouts. He runs to the pile and waves his arms.

Lily and Tom are scared. They hear the farmer and see him. They jump off the pile and run away.

"Sorry, mister, we did not know!" Lily says.

"Me too, sorry!" Tom says.

But the farmer is still angry. He kicks the pile of wheat. He makes a big mess. He grumbles and picks up the wheat.

Lily and Tom are safe. They run to their homes. They are alert. They do not want to play with wheat again. They look for other things to play with.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big puddle. They wanted to jump in it.

"Let's jump in the puddle!" Lily said.

"OK!" Tom said.

They ran to the puddle and jumped in. Splash! They got very wet. They laughed and jumped again.

A lady was walking by. She had a big hat and a long dress. She did not see the puddle. She stepped in it. Splash! She got very wet too. She was not happy.

"Hey!" she said. "What are you doing? You made me wet!"

Lily and Tom stopped jumping. They looked at the lady. They were sorry.

"We are sorry, lady," Lily said. "We did not see you. We were playing."

The lady looked at them. She saw their wet clothes and their wet faces. She saw their big eyes and their small mouths. She guessed they did not mean to make her wet. She guessed they were just having fun.

She sighed. She smiled. She said, "It's OK. I guess it was an accident. But next time, be careful. You might make someone else wet."

Lily and Tom nodded. They said, "OK, lady. We will be careful. Thank you for being nice."

The lady nodded. She said, "You're welcome. Have a good day."

She walked away. She was still wet. But she was not angry.

Lily and Tom looked at each other. They smiled. They said, "Let's play some more!"

They ran to the slide. They slid down. They had fun. They were wet. But they were happy.

"Can we go home, Mom?" Mia asks. She shivers in her coat and hat. "I'm cold and hungry."

"Not yet, sweetie," Mom says. "We have to go to the store first. We need some food and milk."

Tom and Mia follow Mom to the store. They see many cars and buses and people on the street. Some people look happy, some look sad, some look messy. Tom and Mia wonder what their stories are.

"Look, Mom, a clown!" Tom says. He points to a man with a red nose and a colorful suit. He is holding a bunch of balloons and making funny faces.

"Hello, kids!" the clown says. He walks over to them and gives them each a balloon. "Do you like my balloons? They are magic!"

"Magic?" Mia says. She likes magic. She hopes the balloon can make her warm and cozy.

Tom and Mia look at each other. They think of what they wish for. They hold their balloons tight and close their eyes.

"Thank you, clown!" they say.

"You're welcome, kids!" the clown says. He waves and walks away.

Mom takes Tom and Mia's hands and leads them to the store. She buys some food and milk and pays the cashier. Then they go back to the park.

"Look, Mom, our balloons are glowing!" Tom says. He sees a soft light coming from his balloon.

"Wow, so are mine!" Mia says. She sees the same light from her balloon.

Mom looks at their balloons and smiles. She doesn't see the light, but she believes in magic.

They get to the car and get in. Mom turns on the heater and the radio. Tom and Mia feel warm and happy. They look at their balloons and whisper their wishes.

"I wish we can have a nice dinner and a good night's sleep," Tom says.

"I wish we can have a sunny day and a fun adventure tomorrow," Mia says.

They don't know if their wishes will come true, but they feel hopeful and grateful. They hug their balloons and each other. They love their mom and their dog and their city. They are a happy family.

One night, Ben had a dream. He saw a bright light in his room. He opened his eyes and saw an angel. The angel had big wings and a smile. She looked like his mom, but more shiny.

"Hello, Ben," the angel said. "I am here to help you."

Ben was scared and curious. He did not know what to say. He nodded his head.

The angel came closer and touched his cheek. "Don't be afraid, Ben. I love you very much. I know you miss your mom, but she is getting better. She will come home soon. You have to be brave and strong for her."

Ben felt a warm and happy feeling in his heart. He smiled and hugged the angel. "I love you too, angel. Thank you for helping me. Can you stay with me?"

The angel nodded her head. "I will always be with you, Ben. In your dreams and in your heart. You are a special boy and I am proud of you. Now, go back to sleep and have sweet dreams."

The angel kissed his forehead and faded away. Ben closed his eyes and fell asleep. He dreamed of his mom and the angel. He felt less sad and more hopeful.

The next morning, his dad woke him up. He had good news. His mom was better and they could go see her. Ben was very happy. He jumped out of bed and got ready. He felt the angel's presence and thanked her silently.

He ran to his dad and hugged him. "Dad, I had a dream. I saw an angel. She looked like mom. She said mom is getting better and she loves me."

His dad smiled and nodded his head. "That's wonderful, Ben. Maybe the angel was your mom's guardian angel. She was watching over her and you. She loves you very much, too. Come on, let's go see her."

Ben and his dad got in the car and drove to the hospital. The sky was gloomy and gray, but Ben did not mind. He knew the sun was shining behind the clouds. He knew his mom was waiting for him. He knew the angel was with him. He was happy.

The next day, Jack and his mom came back to the same spot. This time Jack had a better plan and he put some corn on the ground. The great parrot flew down to eat the corn and Jack was able to catch him.

Jack was happy and he took the parrot home. He named the parrot "Cupid" and they became best friends. Every day Cupid would fly around and sing. Jack was so proud of his great parrot.

When he got there he couldn't believe his eyes. A beautiful present with a brown bow was waiting for him. The bear was so happy he jumped for joy! He grabbed the present and hugged it tight. 

The bear was so excited that he couldn't wait to open his present. He carefully unwrapped it to find a big, pink bubble wand! He was so delighted that he started laughing and floating around in happy bubbles. He had finally found the perfect present after all his hard work.

As he flew around, the eagle noticed the sock had the power to make him fly even higher. He circled around and around, faster and faster. He was so high up, he could see the whole world below. 

The mighty eagle flew around the world becoming as fast as the wind. He was so proud of himself. He flew with the sock as long as he could, before he flew down and placed it safely onto the ground. 

The eagle smiled to himself and thanked the sock for allowing him to soar. He flew home, feeling mighty and proud. The end.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. Jack had a stove and Jill was jealous. Every day Jack would cook food on the stove and it made Jill very mad.

One day Jill had an idea, she wanted to get back at Jack. So Jill snuck into Jack's house and found the stove. She took out her scissors and carefully started to cut it.

Jack came home, saw the stove and was so angry! He yelled at Jill, but she just ran away.

The next day Jack fixed the stove and started to cook again. Jill was still very jealous, but she wasn't brave enough to cut the stove again.

The moral of the story is don't be jealous of your friends and don't be mean to them.

With wide eyes, the bird flew around it for what seemed like hours, admiring its beauty. He finally flew away, wishing he could be like the giraffe, as happy and carefree as it seemed.

The next day, Timmy went back to the park and found his stick! He was so happy and ran back home to show his mom. She was proud of him for using his notebook to keep track of his stuff. From that day on, Timmy always recorded the things he collected and never lost anything again.

Once upon a time, there was a little cat named Mittens. Mittens loved to play with her ball of yarn and chase after butterflies. One day, Mittens met a big scary dog named Max. Max had a big paw and a loud bark.

Mittens was scared of Max and wanted to leave, but Max said, "Wait, don't be afraid. I just want to be friends." Mittens thought for a moment and decided to give Max a chance.

They played together and had lots of fun. Mittens learned that sometimes things that seem scary can turn out to be good. Mittens and Max became good friends and they never judged each other by their size or looks.

The moral of the story is to never judge someone by their appearance and to always give someone a chance to be your friend.

"I don't want to put my toys away," Lily said.

Lily sighed and started putting her toys in the box. She found it was actually fun to organize them. When she was done, she looked at her tidy room and smiled.

"Wow, this looks great!" she said.

From then on, Lily made sure to put her toys away in the box every day.

She takes out the knife and the spoon from mom's bag. She tries to cut the avocado. But it is too hard. She can't cut it. She pushes harder. The knife slips. She cuts her finger. She cries.

Mom hears her cry. She runs to her. She sees the blood on her finger. She takes a tissue and wraps it around her finger. She hugs her and kisses her.

"Shh, shh, shh. It's okay, Sara. It's just a small cut. It will heal soon. You are brave," mom says.

Sara stops crying. She looks at her finger. She sees the tissue. She feels better. She smiles.

"Thank you, mom. I love you," Sara says.

"I love you too, Sara. Next time, let me help you with the avocado, okay?" mom says.

"Okay, mom. Can I still eat it?" Sara says.

"Of course, you can. Let's go home and make some guacamole. Do you know what that is?" mom says.

"No, what is it?" Sara says.

"It's a yummy dip made with avocados, tomatoes, onions and lime. You can eat it with chips or bread. Do you want to try it?" mom says.

"Yes, I do. That sounds good. Let's go home, mom," Sara says.

They pack their things and leave the park. Sara holds mom's hand. She still has the avocado in her sack. She is excited to try the guacamole. She thinks avocados are hard but tasty. She likes them.

"What is battery?" Lily asks.

"Battery is what makes the car work," Ben says. "It is like food for the car. When the battery is empty, the car is tired and quiet."

"Oh," Lily says. "How do we make the battery full again?"

"We need to find new batteries," Ben says. "Or we can ask mom or dad to help us."

Lily and Ben go to find mom or dad. They learn that batteries are important for some toys. They also learn to share and take turns with the car. They play with the car again, but not too loud. They have fun and are happy.

Lily and Ben were playing in the attic. They found a big chest with a lock. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Maybe there are toys or books or clothes," Lily said.

"Or maybe there are jewels or coins or candy," Ben said.

They looked for a key, but they could not find one. They saw a hammer and a screwdriver on a shelf.

"Let's use these to open the chest," Ben said. He took the hammer and hit the lock hard.

"Wait, Ben, that's not a good idea," Lily said. "That's not our chest. We should ask Mom or Dad first."

But Ben did not listen. He hit the lock again and again, until it broke. He opened the chest and smiled.

"Look, Lily, I was right! There are jewels and coins and candy!" He grabbed a handful and put them in his pocket.

Lily felt scared. She knew they did something wrong. She wanted to tell Ben to stop, but he was too excited.

"Come on, Lily, choose some for yourself. There are plenty for both of us," he said.

Lily shook her head. She did not want to take anything. She wanted to go back downstairs.

"Ben, please, let's go. We should not touch these things. They belong to someone else. Maybe they are very important or very old or very special," she said.

But Ben did not care. He took more and more, until his pockets were full. He closed the chest and ran to the stairs.

"Come on, Lily, hurry up. We can hide these in our room and play with them later," he said.

Lily followed him, but she felt bad. She wished they never found the chest.

They ran down the stairs, but they did not see Mom and Dad waiting for them. They looked angry and sad.

"Ben, Lily, what have you done?" Mom asked. She saw the jewels and coins and candy falling out of Ben's pockets.

"We found a chest in the attic and we opened it and we took some things," Ben said.

"That chest was your great-grandma's. She left it for us when she died. It had her most precious memories and gifts. You broke the lock and stole her things. How could you?" Dad asked.

Ben and Lily felt ashamed. They realized they made a big mistake. They wanted to say sorry, but it was too late.

Mom and Dad took them to their room and locked the door. They said they were very disappointed and angry. They said they had to think about a punishment.

Ben and Lily cried. They wished they listened to Lily and asked Mom or Dad first. They wished they did not choose to be greedy and selfish. They learned a difficult lesson: respect other people's things and always tell the truth.

The rabbit said, "I'm okay, let's keep running!" But the other animals said, "No, we will wait for you. We are a team and we will finish the race together."

So, they all walked together until they saw a big, scary bear. The bear was angry and started chasing them. The team tried to run away, but the bear was too fast. Sadly, the bear caught them all and ate them for dinner. The end.

At first it was hard, but after a few moments Mary got into it. She filled the page with beautiful colors and shapes. When she was done, she smiled with pride at her independent task. She had done it all by herself!

Her mom came outside and asked what happened. "The pine cone slapped me!" Lily said. 

Her mom smiled and said, "Well, sometimes even friends can accidentally hurt each other. But it's important to forgive and move on. Just like you did with the pine tree." 

Lily nodded and went back to playing, happy to have learned a valuable lesson about forgiveness and friendship.

"Thank you, mister," Lily and Tom said. "We are okay, but we are dizzy and we have boo-boos."

"I'm sorry, Sue, I was stubborn," Tom said. "Do you want to go on the slide with me?"

Sue smiled and nodded. She wiped her tears and held Tom's hand.

"OK, Tom, let's go on the slide," Sue said. "But next time, you can go on the big swing if you want."

Tom and Sue went on the slide and had fun. They were friends again.

Tom and Lily were restless. They wanted to play outside, but it was raining. They looked at their toys, but they were bored of them. They wished they had something new and fun to do.

"Let's play with the magic wand!" Lily said. She found the wand in a box of old things. It was shiny and had a star on the end. "Maybe it can do something cool!"

"Okay, let's try it!" Tom said. He took the wand and pointed it at the sofa. He said, "Sofa, shrink!" Nothing happened. He pointed it at the lamp. He said, "Lamp, shrink!" Nothing happened. He pointed it at Lily. He said, "Lily, shrink!"

Lily felt a tickle. She looked at her hands and feet. They were getting smaller and smaller. She screamed, "Tom, stop! You're making me shrink!"

Tom was shocked. He dropped the wand. He ran to Lily. He tried to pick her up, but she was too tiny. He said, "Lily, I'm sorry! I didn't know it would work! How can I make you big again?"

Lily was scared. She saw a big spider crawling near her. She said, "Tom, help! There's a spider! Quick, find the wand!"

Tom looked around. He saw the wand on the floor. He reached for it, but it was too far. He saw a pool of water on the table. It was from a glass that he spilled. He had an idea. He said, "Lily, jump on the pool! Maybe it will make you grow!"

Lily saw the pool. It was like a lake to her. She was afraid of the water, but she was more afraid of the spider. She said, "Okay, I'll try!" She ran to the pool and jumped in.

The water was cold and wet. She felt a splash. She felt another tickle. She looked at her hands and feet. They were getting bigger and bigger. She said, "Tom, it's working! I'm growing!"

Tom was happy. He saw Lily coming out of the pool. She was still wet, but she was normal size. He said, "Lily, you're back! I'm so glad! I'm sorry I made you shrink!"

Lily hugged Tom. She said, "Tom, it's okay. I'm not mad. I'm just glad you saved me! That was a scary adventure!"

They looked at the wand. They decided to put it back in the box. They said, "Let's never play with the magic wand again!" They went to dry themselves and find something else to do. They hoped the rain would stop soon.

Lena was a lively girl who liked to play and sing. She had a big sister, Sara, who was getting married soon. Sara had a beautiful white veil that she would wear on her wedding day. Lena wanted to try on the veil and pretend to be a bride too.

One day, when Sara was not at home, Lena sneaked into her room and found the veil on the bed. She put it on her head and looked at herself in the mirror. She felt very pretty and happy. She started to rock back and forth, humming a song. She did not notice that the veil was getting caught on the bedpost.

Suddenly, she heard Sara's voice outside the door. "Lena, what are you doing in my room?" Sara asked, sounding angry. Lena got scared and tried to run away, but the veil was stuck. She pulled hard and ripped the veil in half. She dropped it on the floor and ran to her room, crying.

Sara came in and saw the torn veil. She was very sad and angry. She had saved a lot of money to buy the veil and now it was ruined. She went to Lena's room and knocked on the door. "Lena, how could you do this? You know how much this veil means to me. You are very naughty and selfish. You have to say sorry and help me fix it." Sara said, sternly.

Lena opened the door and looked at Sara with tearful eyes. She felt very sorry and ashamed. She knew she had done a bad thing. She hugged Sara and said, "I'm sorry, Sara. I just wanted to be like you. You are so pretty and happy. I love you, Sara. Please don't be mad at me. I will help you fix the veil. I will do anything to make you happy."

Sara hugged Lena back and said, "I love you too, Lena. I know you didn't mean to hurt me. You are also pretty and happy, in your own way. You don't have to be like me. You have to be yourself. And you have to respect other people's things. You can't take them without asking. That is not nice. Do you understand?"

Lena nodded and said, "I understand, Sara. I'm sorry. I will never do it again. Can we still be friends?"

Sara smiled and said, "Of course we can. You are my sister and my friend. Come on, let's go and see if we can fix the veil together. Maybe we can make it even more beautiful."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of respect, honesty, apology, forgiveness, and love. It shows that taking other people's things without permission is wrong and can cause harm. It also shows that everyone is unique and special, and does not have to imitate others. It also shows that siblings can overcome conflicts and help each other.

"Zzzzzz!" Ben says.

Sara likes to play in the park with her mom and dad. She likes to see the birds, the flowers and the trees. She also likes to see the animals that live in the park. Sometimes she sees squirrels, rabbits and ducks. She likes to call them and give them some bread.

One day, Sara saw a new animal in the park. It was big and brown and had a long nose. It was eating some grass near the pond. Sara was very curious and wanted to see it better. She asked her mom, "What is that animal, mom?"

Mom said, "That is an elephant, Sara. It is a very big and strong animal. It can use its nose to pick up things and spray water. It is not from here. It is from a far away place. It is here for a visit with some other elephants. They are in a big truck over there."

Sara wanted to go and see the other elephants. She asked her dad, "Can we go and see the elephants, dad?"

Dad said, "Yes, we can, Sara. But we have to be careful and not get too close. The elephants are not used to people and they might get scared or angry. We have to stay behind the fence and not touch them or feed them. We can just look and call them and say hello."

Sara nodded and followed her dad to the fence. She saw four more elephants in the truck. They were different sizes and colors. Some had big ears and some had small ears. Some had long tusks and some had short tusks. Sara thought they were very beautiful and interesting. She called them and said, "Hello, elephants! I am Sara. I like you. You are very big and nice. Where are you from?"

The elephants heard Sara and looked at her. They made some loud noises with their noses. They sounded like trumpets. Sara laughed and clapped her hands. She thought they were talking to her. She said, "What are you saying, elephants? I don't understand. Can you teach me your words?"

The elephants made some more noises and moved their noses. They seemed to like Sara. They were very nosy and wanted to know more about her. They stretched their noses over the fence and tried to touch her. Sara was not afraid. She reached out her hand and touched their noses. They felt rough and wet. She said, "Your noses are funny, elephants. They are very long and soft. Can you do tricks with them?"

The elephants nodded and showed Sara some tricks. They picked up some sticks and stones and threw them in the air. They sprayed some water from the pond and made a rainbow. They wrapped their noses around each other and hugged. Sara was amazed and happy. She said, "Wow, elephants! You are very smart and fun. You can do many things with your noses. I wish I had a nose like yours."

The elephants smiled and shook their heads. They said, "No, Sara. You don't need a nose like ours. You have a nose that is perfect for you. You can smell and breathe and sneeze with your nose. You can also kiss and smile and sing with your nose. You are very special and sweet. We like you just the way you are."

Sara smiled and thanked the elephants. She said, "Thank you, elephants. You are very kind and friendly. I like you just the way you are, too. You are the best animals I ever met. I hope you have a good visit and a safe trip back to your home. Goodbye, elephants. I will miss you."

The elephants waved their noses and said goodbye to Sara. They said, "Goodbye, Sara. We will miss you, too. You are the best human we ever met. You are very brave and curious and nosy. You made us happy and proud. We hope you have a good day and a happy life. Take care, Sara. We love you."

Sara hugged her mom and dad and said, "I love you, too, elephants. And I love you, mom and dad. This was the best day ever. Can we come back to the park tomorrow and see the animals again?"

Mom and dad smiled and said, "Yes, Sara. We can come back to the park tomorrow and see the animals again. Maybe we will see some new animals or some old friends. You never know what you will find in the park. The park is full of surprises and wonders. And so are you, Sara. You are our little wonder and our big surprise. We are very lucky and happy to have you, Sara. You are our nosy, lovely, amazing Sara."

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in the kitchen. They wanted to be chefs like their mom and dad. One day, they found a big jar of pepper on the counter. They opened it and smelled it. It made them sneeze.

"Let's make some soup with pepper," Ben said. "It will be yummy and spicy."

"Okay," Anna said. "But we have to be careful. Mom and dad said not to touch the stove. It is hot and dangerous."

They took a big pot and filled it with water. They put it on the stove, but they did not turn it on. They added some carrots, potatoes, and salt. Then they poured a lot of pepper into the pot. They stirred it with a wooden spoon.

"Look, we made soup!" Anna said. "It smells good."

"Let's taste it," Ben said. He took a spoonful of soup and put it in his mouth. He spat it out right away. It was too spicy. It burned his tongue. He cried.

"Ow, ow, ow!" he said. "It hurts! It hurts!"

Anna wanted to help him. She ran to the fridge to get some milk. But she did not see the rug on the floor. She stumbled and fell. She hurt her knee. She cried too.

"Ow, ow, ow!" she said. "It hurts! It hurts!"

Mom and dad heard their cries. They came to the kitchen and saw the mess. They saw the pot of soup, the jar of pepper, the spilled milk, and the twins on the floor.

"What happened here?" mom asked.

"We wanted to make soup with pepper," Anna said. "But it was too spicy and we got hurt."

Mom and dad hugged them and kissed their wounds. They gave them some water and ice cream to cool their mouths and knees.

"I'm sorry, mom and dad," Ben said. "We should have listened to you. We should not have played with the stove and the pepper."

"I'm sorry too," Anna said. "We should have been more careful. We should not have run in the kitchen."

Mom and dad smiled and said, "It's okay. We forgive you. We know you were curious and wanted to have fun. But you have to remember that some things are not for playing. They are for grown-ups. They can be dangerous or harmful. You have to ask us before you use them. And you have to be safe and respectful in the kitchen. It is not a playground. It is a place to cook and eat."

The twins nodded and said, "We understand. We will do better next time. We love you, mom and dad."

Mom and dad said, "We love you too, Anna and Ben. You are our little chefs. But you still have a lot to learn. Maybe next time we can make soup together. But with less pepper."

The twins laughed and said, "Yes, please. That sounds good."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the children to listen to their parents, to be careful and respectful in the kitchen, and to avoid playing with dangerous or harmful things. It also shows the importance of forgiveness and love.

The blue jay flies to the bike and tries to ring the bell. But the bell is too hard and heavy. The blue jay can not move it. He pushes and pecks and flaps. He makes a lot of noise and mess. He gets tired and frustrated.

The raven watches and smiles. He knows a secret. He has a plan. He has been to the bike before. He has seen how it works. He has learned how to ring the bell. He waits for the right moment.

When the blue jay gives up and flies away, the raven flies to the bike. He lands on the seat. He looks at the bell. He sees a small blue button on the side. He presses the button with his beak. The bell rings loud and clear. The raven says, "I win. I win. I am a real bird. I have color and song. I have skills and tricks. I have manners and friends. You lose. You lose. You are rude and mean. You have no proof and no challenge. You have no game and no fun."

Tom met a navy man named Jack. Jack saw Tom playing with the toy gun. Jack said, "Hi, Tom! Do you like to shoot?" Tom said, "Yes, I do! I want to be in the navy like you!" Jack smiled and said, "Keep practicing, Tom. Maybe one day you can join the navy too!" Tom was very happy and kept playing with his toy gun, dreaming of the day he could be in the navy.

Tim went to his friends' houses. He said, "I have cookies to sell!" His friends were happy. They bought cookies from Tim. Tim was very proud of his brilliant idea. And they all enjoyed the yummy cookies together.

One day, a little girl named Lily found a big box in her room. The box was blue and had pretty pictures on it. Lily was very happy and wanted to see what was inside the box.

Lily opened the box and found a sweet, small cat inside. The cat was soft and had a long tail. The cat waved its tail and said, "Hello, my name is Kitty. Will you be my friend?" Lily smiled and said, "Yes, I will be your friend, Kitty!"

Together, Lily and Kitty played all day. They waved at the birds outside the window and shared sweet treats from the box. When the sun went down, they were both very tired. Lily gave Kitty a big hug and they went to sleep, happy to have found a new friend.

Once upon a time, in a big park, there was a little ant named Tim. Tim was a fearful ant. He was scared of everything. One day, Tim went out to find food for his family.

Tim saw a big tree with lots of shade. He thought it was a good place to rest. Under the tree, Tim found a pinch of food. He was so happy! But then, he saw a big bug. The big bug wanted to pinch Tim.

Tim was very scared, but he had an idea. He ran into the shade and hid behind a leaf. The big bug could not find Tim. Tim felt safe in the shade. After the big bug left, Tim took the food and went back to his family. Tim was a brave ant now.

Max saw a squirrel and wanted to play with it. He ran after the squirrel and did not see Jane. Jane called for Max, but he did not come back. Jane was very sad. Max could not escape from the squirrel. He was lost and could not find his way back home.

"Max, where are you?" Jane cried. But Max was too far away to hear her. He was scared and missed his family. Jane and her mom looked for Max, but they could not find him.

The sky got dark, and it was time to go home. Jane and her mom had to leave the park without Max. They were very sad. Max was still lost and could not find his way back home.

Fin and his friends wanted to give the flag to their friend, Sally the seahorse. They thought Sally would like it because the flag was her favorite color, red. So, they worked together to carry the flag to Sally's home.

When they gave the flag to Sally, she was so happy! She said, "Thank you, friends!" and put the flag in front of her home. Now, every time Fin and his friends swam by Sally's home, they saw the red flag and remembered the fun they had giving it to her. And they all lived happily ever after.

"Bob, don't eat the mint!" Tim said. "It might not be good for you."

But Bob didn't listen. He thought it would taste good, so he took a bite. Suddenly, his tummy started to hurt. He felt bad for not listening to Tim.

Bob said, "I'm sorry, Tim. I should have listened to you. Can you help me feel better?"

Tim nodded and went to find some water for Bob. When Bob drank the water, he started to feel better. He learned to listen to his friends and not to eat things without knowing if they are good for him.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a drawer in his room. In the drawer, he kept all his toys. Tim's toys were very obedient. They always stayed in the drawer when Tim was not playing with them.

One day, Tim's mom told him, "Tim, you need to unite all your toys and put them back in the drawer before dinner." Tim said, "Okay, Mommy!" He went to his room and started to pick up his toys.

As Tim put his toys in the drawer, he noticed that one toy was missing. It was his favorite toy, a little red car. Tim looked all around his room, but he could not find the car. He felt sad and worried.

Then, Tim heard a small voice. It was his toy robot! The robot said, "Tim, I know where your car is. It is hiding under your bed!" Tim looked under his bed and found his little red car. He was so happy!

Tim thanked the robot and put all his toys back in the drawer. He united all his obedient toys in the drawer, just like his mom had asked. Tim had a big smile on his face as he went to dinner with his family.

Tom was a young boy who liked to help his dad with the wood. His dad had a big axe that he used to chop the wood. Tom wanted to use the axe too, but his dad said it was too sharp and heavy for him.

One day, Tom saw the axe lying on the ground near the woodpile. He thought his dad was not looking, so he ran to the axe and tried to lift it. But the axe was too heavy for him, and he dropped it on a rock. The axe made a loud clang and the blade broke.

Tom was scared and sad. He broke his dad's axe. He did not know what to do. He hid the axe behind some bushes and ran to his room.

His dad heard the clang and went to see what happened. He saw the broken axe and the rock. He knew Tom had tried to use the axe. He was angry and worried. He went to Tom's room and knocked on the door.

"Tom, come out. I need to talk to you," his dad said.

Tom opened the door and looked at his dad. He saw his dad's angry face and felt sorry.

"Dad, I'm sorry. I broke your axe. I wanted to help you with the wood. I did not mean to break it," Tom said.

His dad sighed and hugged him.

"Tom, I'm glad you are sorry. But you should not touch my axe. It is dangerous and not for you. You could have hurt yourself or someone else. You need to be careful and listen to me," his dad said.

"I know, dad. I'm sorry. I won't touch your axe again. Can you fix it?" Tom asked.

His dad smiled and nodded.

"Yes, I can fix it. I can repair it with some glue and a new handle. But you have to help me. You have to find the broken piece and bring it to me. And you have to promise me you will never touch my axe again," his dad said.

"I promise, dad. I will help you. I will find the broken piece and bring it to you. And I will never touch your axe again," Tom said.

Tom and his dad went to the woodpile and found the broken piece. They took it to the shed and repaired the axe. They worked together and had fun. Tom learned how to repair things and his dad forgave him. They hugged and said they loved each other. They were happy.

One day, Lily has a new pen. It is big and red. It has thick ink. Lily says, "Look, Tom, I have a new pen. It is very good. It makes thick lines. Do you want to try?"

But then, something bad happens. The pen breaks. The ink spills out. It makes a big mess. The ink is on the paper, on the table, on the floor and on Tom's hands. Tom is scared. He says, "Oh no! The pen is broken. The ink is everywhere. What do we do?"

Lily is scared too. She says, "We have to run. We have to hide. Mom will be angry. She will see the ink. She will not like it." She grabs Tom's hand. They run to the closet. They hide inside. They hope Mom will not find them. They are sorry for the mess. They are sorry for the pen. They are not happy.

Sam and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to make loud noises and pretend they were animals or cars or superheroes. They did not hear their mom calling them from the kitchen.

"Sam! Lily! Dinner is ready!" Mom said. She sounded serious. She did not like it when they ignored her. She put the plates on the table and went to find them.

She saw them on the floor, surrounded by toys. They were still making noises and having fun. She frowned and said, "Sam, Lily, I told you dinner is ready. You need to stop playing and come eat. Now."

Sam and Lily looked at each other. They knew Mom was serious. They did not want to make her angry. They also liked dinner. It smelled good. They decided to obey Mom and put away their toys.

They ran to the kitchen and sat on their chairs. They said, "Sorry, Mom. We did not hear you. We were playing."

Mom smiled and said, "It's okay. I know you were playing. But you need to listen when I call you. Dinner is important. It is good for you. And we can talk and share our day."

Sam and Lily nodded and said, "Okay, Mom. We will listen next time. We love you. And we love dinner."

Mom hugged them and said, "I love you too. And I love dinner. Now, let's eat."

Tom and Mia are playing with their toy cars in the living room. They have a big box of cars of different colors and sizes. They like to make roads and bridges with their blocks and pretend to drive around.

"Look, I have a green car!" Mia says, holding up a shiny toy. "It is very fast and pretty."

"I have a green car too!" Tom says, showing his own toy. "But mine is bigger and louder. It can go over anything!"

They start to race their cars on the floor, making vroom and beep sounds. They have fun, but they also want to win. They try to push each other's cars out of the way.

"Hey, stop that!" Mia says, as Tom bumps her car with his. "You are cheating!"

"No, I'm not!" Tom says, as Mia nudges his car with hers. "You are cheating!"

They get angry and start to fight. They grab each other's cars and throw them across the room. The cars scatter everywhere, hitting the walls and the furniture. Some of them break and lose their wheels.

"Stop, stop, stop!" Mom says, coming into the living room. She sees the mess and the broken toys. She is not happy. "What are you doing? Why are you throwing your cars?"

Tom and Mia look at Mom. They feel sorry and ashamed. They don't know what to say.

Mom sighs and picks up the cars. She puts them back in the box. She finds a switch on the wall and turns it on. The lights go off.

"Time for bed," Mom says. "You have played enough. You need to rest and say sorry to each other."

Tom and Mia nod and hug each other. They say sorry and give each other their cars. They follow Mom to their bedroom. They brush their teeth and put on their pajamas. They get into their beds and snuggle with their cars.

"Good night, Tom," Mia says.

"Good night, Mia," Tom says.

They close their eyes and fall asleep. They dream of green cars and happy races.

Tom likes to play with his toy cars. He has many cars of different colors and sizes. He likes to make them zoom and crash on the floor. His favorite car is a big red truck with a loud motor. He calls it Big Red.

One day, Tom's mom tells him to bring Big Red to the park. She says they will meet his friend Sam there. Tom is happy. He likes to play with Sam. He puts Big Red in his backpack and goes with his mom to the park.

At the park, Tom sees Sam waiting for him. Sam has a blue car with a shiny hood. He calls it Bluey. Tom and Sam say hello and take out their cars. They start to race them on the grass. Big Red is faster than Bluey. Tom is proud of his car.

But then, something bad happens. Big Red starts to slow down. Its motor makes a funny noise. It stops moving. Tom is sad. He tries to make it go again, but it does not work. He thinks his car is broken.

Bunny was a little rabbit who loved to hop around the meadow. He liked to explore new places and meet new friends. One day, he saw a big pond with shiny water and green plants. He wanted to hop closer and see what was inside.

But Frog, who lived in the pond, did not like strangers. He saw Bunny hopping near his home and croaked loudly. "Who are you and what do you want?" he asked in a grumpy voice.

Bunny was scared and anxious. He did not know how to answer Frog's question. He thought Frog might be angry or mean. He wanted to hop away, but he also wanted to be polite. He said in a small voice, "I am Bunny and I just want to look at the pond. It is very pretty."

Frog was surprised by Bunny's answer. He realized that Bunny was not a threat, but a curious and friendly visitor. He felt sorry for being rude and decided to be nice. He said in a softer voice, "I am Frog and this is my home. You can look at the pond, but be careful not to fall in. The water is deep and cold."

Bunny was relieved and happy. He thanked Frog and hopped closer to the pond. He saw fish and ducks and water lilies. He asked Frog many questions and learned a lot. Frog answered patiently and shared his knowledge. They became friends and had fun.

Mommy smelled the smoke and ran to the living room. She saw the fire and grabbed a blanket to put it out. She was very scared and angry.

"Lily! Tom! What have you done? You could have burned the house down! How could you play with a candle?" Mommy shouted.

Lily and Tom came back to the living room and saw the mess. They felt very sorry and ashamed. They hugged Mommy and cried.

Mommy hugged them back and calmed down. She was glad they were not hurt, but she was still upset.

"I love you too, Lily and Tom. But you have to listen to me. Candles are not toys. They are for grown-ups only. They can cause fire and hurt people. You have to be more careful and responsible. Do you understand?" Mommy said.

They climb the tree and find some nuts. They are peanuts. They are happy. They start to eat the peanuts.

But then, they hear a loud noise. It is a big bird. It is a hawk. The hawk is hungry. It sees Tom and Sue in the tree. It wants to eat them.

"Help, Sue, a hawk!" Tom says. He is scared. He drops his peanuts.

"Help, Tom, a hawk!" Sue says. She is scared too. She hangs on to a branch.

The hawk is angry. It screeches. It flaps its wings. It shakes the tree.

The tree is old. It cannot hold the hawk. It cracks. It falls. Tom and Sue fall too.

But they are lucky. They land on a soft pile of leaves. They are not hurt. They run away from the hawk.

They are safe. They hug each other. They are glad.

"Wow, Sue, that was scary," Tom says.

"Yes, Tom, that was scary. But we are OK," Sue says.

They look at the tree. It is broken. The peanuts are gone.

"Maybe we can find some more nuts somewhere else," Tom says.

"Maybe, Tom, but not in an old tree," Sue says.

"That's not fair!" Lily said. "You're being rude! We're supposed to share!"

Lily ran after him. She wanted to tell him that he was wrong. She had learned about diamonds in a book. They were not real stones. They were made by people. They were not worth anything in the park. They were only for grown-ups who liked to wear them on their fingers or necks.

She caught up with Ben and shouted at him.

"Ben, wait! Listen to me! That's not a diamond! It's fake! It's just glass!"

"No, it's not! It's a diamond! It's real! You're just jealous!" Ben said.

He held the stone up to his eye and looked at it. He saw the colors of the rainbow. He smiled. He thought it was beautiful.

"You're welcome, sweetie. Be careful, don't spill the water." Her mom said.

"Hey, stop that!" Sara shouted. "You are making the slide wet. That's not nice."

Sara and her mom went to the slide and found the boy. They told him that he was wrong to splash water on the slide and the purse. They asked him to say sorry and stop.

The boy looked at them and said, "Sorry. I was just having fun. I didn't mean to make you mad. I won't do it again."

Sara and her mom accepted his apology and thanked him. They hoped he would be more careful and respectful next time. They decided to go to another part of the park where it was dry and clean. They had fun playing together and forgot about the wet slide and the wet purse.

Ben and Lily liked to play with their toys in the garden. They had a big box of toys with cars, dolls, balls and animals. One day, they found a new toy in the box. It was a sheep. It was white and soft and had a button on its back.

"What does this button do?" Ben asked.

"Let's press it and see," Lily said.

They pressed the button and the sheep made a sound. "Baa, baa," it said. Ben and Lily laughed. They liked the sheep. It was lovely.

They played with the sheep for a long time. They made it run, jump and roll. They gave it grass to eat and water to drink. They hugged it and kissed it. They named it Fluffy.

But they did not know that the button had another function. Every time they pressed it, the sheep shrank a little bit. It was so small that they did not notice at first. But after a while, they saw that the sheep was much smaller than before.

"Look, Fluffy is tiny!" Ben said.

"Oh no, what happened?" Lily said.

They pressed the button again, hoping to make Fluffy bigger. But it did not work. The sheep shrank even more. It was now the size of a mouse.

"Stop, stop, don't press it anymore!" Ben said.

But it was too late. They pressed the button one more time, and Fluffy disappeared. It was gone.

"Where is Fluffy?" Lily cried.

"I don't know, I can't see it," Ben said.

They looked everywhere for Fluffy. They searched the box, the grass, the flowers, the rocks. But they could not find it. They were very sad. They had lost their lovely sheep.

They went inside the house and told their mom what happened. She hugged them and said, "I'm sorry, my dears. Fluffy was a magic sheep. It was a gift from your uncle. He is a magician. He wanted to surprise you with a special toy. But he forgot to tell you how to use it. You have to press the button twice to make it bigger, not once. Once makes it smaller."

"Can we get Fluffy back?" Ben asked.

"Maybe, if we call your uncle. He might know where Fluffy went. Maybe he can bring it back. But you have to be careful with magic toys. They can be tricky. Next time, ask me before you play with them, okay?" Mom said.

"Okay, Mom," Ben and Lily said.

They hoped that their uncle would find Fluffy and bring it back. They missed their lovely sheep. They learned a lesson. They would never press a button without knowing what it does.

It swam fast and hard. It jumped out of the water and bit the net. It tore the net and let all the fish and the reef out. It saw the man who was speaking and laughing. It bit him too. It made him stop.

Ben and Mia saw the shark. They were scared and amazed. They swam away from the boat and the net. They swam back to the shore. They were safe and happy. They thanked the shark for saving the fish and the reef. They hoped that the man would learn his lesson. They hoped that he would never come back.

"Put it here, Ben. It will make the tower stronger. I have a blue block. It is a circle. I will put it on top of your red block." Lily said.

They kept building the tower higher and higher. They were happy and proud of their work. They counted the blocks they used. They knew some numbers, like one, two, three, four, and five.

"Ben, how many blocks do we have?" Lily asked.

"I don't know, Lily. I can't count more than five. Let's ask Mom. She knows all the numbers." Ben said.

They ran to the kitchen, where Mom was making cookies. They asked her to come and see their tower. They wanted her to tell them how many blocks they used.

"Wow, Lily and Ben, you made a very big tower. It is very nice. You used a lot of blocks. Let me see. "Twenty, twenty, twenty. Ha ha ha." They said.

They ran back to their tower. They wanted to play some more. They wanted to make the tower even bigger. They looked for more blocks. They saw a box in the corner. It had a label that said "Supply". They did not know what that meant. They thought it was another funny word. They opened the box. It had more blocks inside. They were happy. They took some blocks and added them to their tower.

But the box did not have blocks for playing. It had blocks for building. They were heavy and hard. They were not meant for children. They were meant for Dad. He was a builder. He used them to make houses and walls. He left them in the corner by mistake. He forgot to put them away.

When Lily and Ben put the heavy blocks on their tower, the tower became unstable. It could not hold the weight. It started to wobble and shake. It fell down with a loud crash. It broke into pieces. It hurt Lily and Ben. They cried and screamed. They had cuts and bruises. They were scared and sad.

He took Lily and Ben to the hospital. They had to get stitches and bandages. They had to stay in bed for a long time. They could not play with blocks anymore.

The moral of the story is: Do not play with things you do not know. They can be dangerous and hurt you. Always ask your parents before you use something new. They can tell you what it is and how to use it safely. They can supply you with the right toys and the right numbers. They can help you have fun and learn. They love you and want you to be happy and healthy.

Her mom shouted "Lila, wait! Don't go near the lion!" But Lila did not listen. She thought the lion was friendly and wanted to play with her.

She reached the cage and said "Hello, lion. Do you want to be my friend? I have a toy lion like you. See?" She held up her toy lion and showed it to the real lion. The real lion saw the toy lion and growled. It did not like the toy lion. It thought it was a rival and wanted to attack it. It jumped at the cage and tried to grab the toy lion.

Lila was scared and dropped her toy lion. The real lion caught the toy lion in its mouth and tore it apart. Lila cried and screamed. Her mom ran to her and hugged her. She said "Lila, I'm sorry. You should have listened to me. The lion is not a friend. It is a wild animal. It can hurt you and your toy. You should never go near a wild animal. You should relax and stay safe."

Lila learned a hard lesson that day. She lost her toy lion and her trust in the real lion. She realized that not all animals are friendly and that she should obey her mom. She wished she had relaxed and played with her toy lion in the park instead of going to the show. She was sad and sorry. The end.

"I ate candy and watched cartoons," Tommy said in a weak voice.

"I'm sorry, mom. I did not know. I thought candy and cartoons were good. But they made me feel bad. I don't want them anymore. I want to be healthy and happy," Tommy said.

"That sounds good, mom. I love you too. Thank you for taking care of me," Tommy said.
