Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play with their toy trucks. They had a big pile of sand in the backyard, and they pretended to be builders. They used their trucks to load and unload the sand, and made roads and hills and castles.

One day, it was very hot and sunny, and they got sweaty and dirty from playing. Their mom called them inside and said, "It's time for a shower, boys. You need to wash off the sand and cool down." But Tom and Sam did not want to stop playing. They said, "No, mom, we want to play more. We are not dirty, we are builders."

Their mom was not happy. She said, "You are not builders, you are boys. And boys need to listen to their mom and take a shower. If you don't, you will get itchy and smelly and have bad dreams. Now come on, or I will take away your trucks."

Tom and Sam did not like that. They did not want to lose their trucks. But they were also restless and wanted to play more. They thought of a plan. They said, "OK, mom, we will take a shower. But can we take our trucks with us? They are dirty too, and they need a shower."

Their mom thought for a moment. She said, "Well, I guess you can, but only if you promise to wash them well and not make a mess in the bathroom. And you have to be quick, because it's almost time for dinner."

Tom and Sam agreed. They ran to the bathroom with their trucks, and turned on the shower. They put their trucks under the water, and pretended to wash them. But they also splashed and sprayed and made a lot of noise. They had fun, but they also made the bathroom wet and sandy.

Their mom heard the noise and came to check on them. She was not happy. She said, "Boys, what are you doing? You are not taking a shower, you are making a mess. Look at the floor, and the walls, and the towels. They are all wet and sandy. And you are still dirty. You did not wash yourselves, you only played with your trucks."

Tom and Sam felt ashamed. They knew they did not listen to their mom, and they did not do what they said. They said, "Sorry, mom, we were having fun. We did not mean to make a mess. We will clean it up, and we will take a real shower."

Their mom said, "You better do that, boys. And next time, when I tell you to do something, you do it. Playing is good, but you also need to take care of yourself and your things. And you need to respect your mom and your home. Do you understand?"

Tom and Sam nodded. They said, "Yes, mom, we understand. We will do better next time. We love you, mom."

Their mom smiled. She said, "I love you too, boys. Now go and take a shower, and then come for dinner. And don't forget to dry your trucks."

The moral of the story is: Listen to your mom and do what she says. Playing is good, but you also need to take care of yourself and your things. And you need to respect your mom and your home.

Mom and Dad and Sam forgave him. They cleaned him and warmed him. They gave him a new sock and a hug. They told him they loved him.

Tom learned his lesson. He never played with scissors or cut things that were not his again. He never went near the chimney again. He was a good boy. He was not bored. He was happy.

Anna tries to untie the knot. She pulls and twists. But the knot is too hard. She cannot untie it.

Tom sees Anna. He wants to help her. He knows how to untie knots. He learned from his dad. He goes to Anna.

"Can I help you?" he asks.

"No, I can do it myself," Anna says. She is jealous. She does not want Tom to untie the knot. She wants to do it herself.

But Tom does not listen. He takes the rope from Anna. He unties the knot. He gives it back to Anna.

"Here you go," he says. "Now you can have some soup."

Anna is angry. She does not say thank you. She does not want the soup. She wants the knot. She snatches the rope from Tom. She ties the knot again. She runs away.

Tom is sad. He does not understand. He only wanted to help. He goes to his mom.

"Why is Anna mad at me?" he asks.

"Sometimes people get jealous when they think someone else is better than them," his mom says. "But you did nothing wrong. You were kind and generous. Maybe Anna will say sorry later."

Tom nods. He hopes Anna will be his friend again. He goes to the man who can cook. He asks for some soup. He shares it with his mom. It is warm and tasty. He smiles.

The giant took the princess on an adventure around the world - they explored snowy mountains, deep oceans, and dense forests. Everywhere they went was more amazing than the last. 

At the end of the day, the giant took the princess back to the palace. He said goodbye and thanked her for such a fun adventure. She smiled and nodded happily. 

Every night the princess looked at the stars and remembered her amazing adventure with the giant. She would never forget it!

Sally smiled because she was so happy that she had won the race. She was also grateful that she had such a lovely family who supported her. She ate her toast and finished first in the race once again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Mary and Jody. Mary and Jody were best friends and loved to play together. 

One day Mary and Jody were playing in Mary's backyard. Mary mentioned to Jody that she wanted to go to a special place. Jody asked Mary where they were going and Mary said they were going to the earth! 

The girls began to dream about what the earth might be like. Jody mentioned that it would be full of purple flowers. Mary thought it might be covered in a bright purple sky.

The two friends got a little scared but still decided to go explore the earth. So, off they went! But when they arrived, what they saw was something quite unexpected. Everywhere they looked there were purple flowers, trees and even buildings covered in a bright purple color! 

Mary and Jody stayed to look around and eventually came home. They told everybody about their exciting adventure and all the wonderful purple things they had seen!

Once upon a time there was a girl who was very worried. She was worried about a story she had heard. When she asked her mum what the story was, her mum only smiled and said nothing.

The girl said again: "Mum, why can't you tell me the story?" 

Her mum replied: "I think it's for you to find out."

The girl was even more worried but decided to look for the story. She asked everyone she knew but nobody could tell her.

Then one day, while she was walking in the garden, she saw an old lady who was smiling. She asked the old lady her question and the old lady replied: 

"Why don't you look up at the stars and tell me a story?" 

The girl looked at the stars and thought of all the stories she knew. She closed her eyes and when she opened them, a big bright star was shining right in front of her. She felt happy knowing that she had found the story she was looking for.

The next morning, Lily woke up and found a shiny coin under her pillow. She was so happy! She sang a song to thank the Tooth Fairy. Her mommy smiled and said, "Your messy room is now clean. You sang a song and got a prize. That's a good setup and payoff!" Lily didn't understand what that meant, but she was happy that she got a surprise and could sing again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, especially his toy car. He would zoom it around the house all day long. One day, Timmy's car stopped moving. He looked at it and saw that the battery was dead. Timmy was sad because he couldn't play with his car anymore.

Timmy's mommy saw him looking sad and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her about his car and the dead battery. His mommy said not to worry and went to get a new battery. Timmy watched as his mommy put the new battery in his car. He was so happy to see his car move again, he couldn't stop gazing at it.

But then, Timmy's little sister came and took his car away. Timmy got angry and started crying. His mommy came over and asked what happened. Timmy told her about his sister taking his car. His mommy talked to his sister and gave Timmy his car back. Timmy was happy again and continued to play with his car all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a big tree with lots of apples. The tree was very happy because it was wealthy in fruits. One day, a little girl came by and asked for an apple. The tree was happy to share and split an apple in half for the girl.

The little girl was so happy with the apple that she wanted to give something back to the tree. She made a loop out of a piece of string and put it on one of the branches. The tree was very grateful and felt even more wealthy now that it had a new decoration.

The moral of the story is that sharing makes us all feel wealthy in our hearts. Even if we split what we have, we can still be happy and make others happy too.

Later that day, Lily's mom made her a sandwich for lunch. As Lily took a bite, she noticed something hard in her mouth. She spit it out and saw that it was a small piece of the vine she had chewed on earlier. She realized that sometimes things that look fun to chew on aren't always good for you. 

From that day on, Lily only chewed on her favorite gum and never on any vines again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the desert with her mom and dad. One day, as they were walking, Lily found a shiny rock. 

"Look what I find!" she said excitedly to her parents.

"That's a pretty rock, Lily," her mom said. "But we need to keep walking. We're trying to find an oasis."

Lily didn't know what an oasis was, but she followed her parents anyway. After a while, they came across a small pond of water surrounded by green plants. 

"Wow, we found an oasis!" Lily exclaimed.

As they were resting by the oasis, Lily noticed a dead bug on the ground. 

"Ew, that bug is dead," she said to her parents.

"Yes, sometimes things die in the desert," her dad explained. "But it's important to appreciate the life we do find, like this oasis." 

Lily nodded, understanding what her dad meant. She was happy they found the oasis and grateful for the adventure they had.

He sits on the piano bench. He puts his hands on the keys. He tries to play a song. But he does not know what to do. He presses the wrong keys. He makes a loud noise. He does not use his feet. He does not look at the paper. He does not hear the sound.

His aunt says, "Tom, stop. You are making a mess. You are not playing the piano. You are just hitting the keys. You have to learn the rules. You have to practice a lot. You have to be patient."

Tom says, "But I want to play the piano. I want to play like you. I want to play beautiful songs."

His aunt says, "I understand. But you have to start with the small piano. You have to learn the easy songs. You have to get better step by step. Then, when you are ready, you can play the big piano. You can play the difficult songs. You can play like me. But you have to work hard. Do you want to do that?"

Tom thinks for a moment. He says, "Yes, I do. I want to work hard. I want to get better. I want to play the piano."

His aunt says, "Good. Then let's go back to your room. I will teach you some songs. I will help you practice. I will be proud of you."

Tom smiles. He says, "Thank you, aunt. You are very kind. You are a good teacher. I love you."

He hugs his aunt. He takes her hand. He goes back to his room. He plays the small piano. He learns some songs. He practices a lot. He gets better. He is happy.

"What's an envelope?" Timmy asked.

"It's like a paper pocket that you put letters in," Lily explained.

Timmy looked at the envelope and said, "I'm not comfortable holding it. Can we stop playing with it?"

Lily agreed and they put the envelope back on the ground. They continued playing and having fun outside. From that day on, Lily and Timmy always made sure to stop and be careful around envelopes they found on the ground.

Suddenly, he heard a voice. "Hello there, little bunny. Are you lost?" It was a wise old owl who lived in the forest. "Yes," said Flopsy, "I'm lost in this maze and I don't know which way to go." The owl replied, "I can help you get out of the maze, but you must surrender to me first."

Flopsy didn't know what "surrender" meant, but he trusted the owl and agreed. The owl led Flopsy through the maze, showing him which way to go. Finally, they reached the end of the maze and Flopsy was so happy to be out. "Thank you, wise old owl!" he exclaimed.

One day, Ben and Mia saw a huge dolphin near the shore. It was bigger than any dolphin they had ever seen. It had a long, pointy nose and a big, curved fin. It looked sad and lonely.

"Hello, dolphin!" Ben shouted. "Do you want to play with us?"

The huge dolphin looked at Ben and Mia. It made a low, sad noise.

"I think he is lost," Mia said. "Maybe he can't find his family."

Ben and Mia felt sorry for the huge dolphin. They wanted to help him.

"Maybe we can unite him with his family," Ben said. "Maybe they are looking for him too."

"How can we do that?" Mia asked.

Ben thought for a moment. He had an idea.

"Maybe we can make a big noise, like the dolphins do. Maybe his family will hear us and come to find him."

Ben and Mia nodded. They took a deep breath and started to make loud, high-pitched noises. They sounded like dolphins.

The huge dolphin heard them. He looked surprised and curious. He made a loud, high-pitched noise back.

Ben and Mia smiled. They kept making noises with the huge dolphin.

Soon, they saw more dolphins coming from the water. They were different sizes and colors, but they all looked happy. They made noises too.

The huge dolphin saw them. He recognized them. They were his family. He swam towards them. They swam towards him. They united.

Ben and Mia watched as the dolphins hugged and kissed each other. They were happy for the huge dolphin. He was not sad and lonely anymore.

"Bye, dolphin!" Ben and Mia shouted. "We are glad you found your family!"

The huge dolphin and his family waved their fins at Ben and Mia. They thanked them for their help. They jumped and splashed in the water. They were happy.

But Tom and Amy did not say thank you. They did not even look at their mom. They just grabbed the tray and put it on the floor. They started to eat the cookies and throw the sandwiches at each other. They made a big mess.

Their mom was very sad. She went to the kitchen and cried. She worked hard to make them a nice lunch, but they did not appreciate it. They did not love her.

Then, something bad happened. The tray was on the floor, and it had a lot of crumbs and bits of food on it. A big rat came out of a hole in the wall and smelled the food. It ran to the tray and started to eat. It was very hungry and greedy.

Tom and Amy saw the rat and screamed. They were scared of the rat. They tried to run away, but the rat was faster. It bit Tom on the leg and Amy on the arm. It hurt a lot. They cried and cried.

Their mom heard them and ran to their room. She saw the rat and the mess and the blood. She was very angry and scared. She grabbed a broom and chased the rat away. She took Tom and Amy to the doctor. They had to get shots and bandages.

They learned a hard lesson. They should have been nice to their mom and enjoyed their lunch. They should have been grateful and polite. They should not have been spoiled children.

Lily was a little girl who liked to poke things. She poked her toys, her books, her cat, and sometimes her brother. She wanted to see what would happen when she poked them. Sometimes they made noises, sometimes they moved, and sometimes they got angry.

One day, Lily saw something new in the bathroom. It was a green bottle with a spray on top. She wondered what was inside. She picked up the bottle and poked the spray. A mist came out and smelled funny. Lily coughed and sneezed. She did not like the smell.

She put the bottle down and ran out of the bathroom. She saw her mom in the kitchen. She told her mom what she did. Her mom was not happy. She told Lily that the bottle was for cleaning the bathroom, not for poking. She said that the mist was bad for Lily's nose and eyes. She took Lily to the sink and washed her face with water.

Lily felt sorry for poking the bottle. She said sorry to her mom. Her mom hugged her and said it was okay. She told Lily to be careful and not poke things that she did not know. She said that some things were not for playing, but for grown-ups. Lily nodded and said she understood. She asked her mom if she could poke her cat instead. Her mom smiled and said yes, but gently. Lily ran to find her cat and poked him softly. He purred and licked her hand. Lily was happy. She liked to poke things, but only the right things.

Sara and Tom were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a big chamber full of toys and books, but they also loved to see the flowers and bugs outside. One day, they found a tiny seed on the ground. It was brown and round and had a little hole in it.

"Look, Sara, what is this?" Tom asked, holding the seed in his hand.

"I don't know, Tom. Maybe it is a flower seed. Let's plant it and see what happens," Sara said, taking the seed from Tom.

They dug a small hole in the dirt and put the seed in it. Then they covered it with more dirt and watered it with a cup. They made a sign with a stick and a paper that said "Our seed" and stuck it next to the hole.

Every day, they came to check on their seed. They watered it and talked to it and sang to it. They hoped it would grow into a beautiful flower. But nothing happened for a long time. The seed stayed hidden under the dirt.

"Maybe our seed is broken," Tom said one day, feeling sad.

"Maybe it needs more time," Sara said, trying to be hopeful.

They decided to wait a little longer and see if their seed would grow.

One morning, they ran to the garden and saw something amazing. There was a green sprout poking out of the dirt. It had two tiny leaves and a bud at the top. It was their seed! It had grown!

"Wow, Sara, look! Our seed is alive!" Tom shouted, jumping up and down.

"Yay, Tom, look! Our seed is a flower!" Sara cheered, clapping her hands.

They hugged each other and danced around their seed. They were so happy and proud. They watched as the bud opened and revealed a bright yellow flower. It was the most adorable flower they had ever seen. It smelled sweet and had a smiley face on it.

"Hello, Sara and Tom. Thank you for taking care of me. I am your friend, Sunny," the flower said, blinking its eyes.

"Hello, Sunny. We are your friends, too. You are the best flower ever," Sara and Tom said, smiling back.

They gave Sunny a kiss and a hug and told him they loved him. They played with him and told him stories and jokes. They had a lot of fun with their new friend. They learned that seeds can grow into wonderful things if you are patient and kind. They were very happy.

He ran to the gate and tried to open it. He pulled and pushed and kicked, but the gate did not move. He saw a hole in the gate. He put his hand through the hole and felt something hot.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Tom screamed. He pulled his hand back and saw it was red and hurt. He had burned his hand.

Lily ran to him and hugged him. She saw his hand and was scared.

"Tom, you're hurt! You're hurt bad! We need to tell Mommy!" Lily said.

She helped him walk to the house. They saw Mommy in the kitchen. She saw Tom's hand and was shocked.

"Tom, what happened? What did you do?" Mommy asked.

"I touched the fire behind the gate. It was terrible. It burned me." Tom said.

Mommy took him to the sink and ran cold water over his hand. She wrapped it in a cloth and gave him a hug and a kiss.

"You were very naughty, Tom. You should never touch fire. It's very dangerous. It can hurt you and make you sick. You should always listen to Mommy and Lily. They love you and want you to be safe." Mommy said.

"I'm sorry, Mommy. I'm sorry, Lily. I won't touch fire again. I love you too." Tom said.

Mommy smiled and said, "I'm glad you're sorry. I hope you learned your lesson. Now let's go to the doctor and see if your hand needs medicine."

But no one heard them. Their mom and dad were busy talking to their friends. They did not see Lila and Tom running into the water.

The water was deep and cold. Lila and Tom could not swim. They felt helpless and scared. They tried to hold on to each other, but the wave pulled them apart.

They sank under the water and did not come up again.

The moral of the story is: Do not go into the water without an adult. It is dangerous and you can drown.

After they played for a while, Tim saw that Sue's toy was not a microscope, but a telescope. Tim was sad because they did not match. He told Sue, "Our toys are not the same, so I cannot play with you anymore." Sue was sad too, and they both went home.

The next day, Tim's mom told him that it was not nice to leave Sue just because their toys did not match. Tim felt bad and went back to the park to say sorry to Sue. But Sue was not there. Tim never saw Sue again and he was very sad.

The moral of the story is to not judge friends by what they have, but by who they are.

Once upon a time, in a quiet little town, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside with his friends. They would run, jump, and laugh all day long. Tim's favorite thing to do was to pass a ball with his friends.

One sunny day, while Tim and his friends were playing, they saw a big pear tree. The tree was full of big, juicy pears. Tim's friend, Sue, said, "Let's pick some pears and eat them!" Tim and his friends agreed, and they all went to the tree.

As they picked the pears, they talked and laughed. Tim said, "These pears look so yummy!" Sue replied, "Yes, they do! Let's share them with everyone!" So, they passed the pears to each other and ate them together. The pears were sweet and juicy, and the children enjoyed them very much.

After they finished eating the pears, they continued to play and pass the ball. They had a great time under the quiet, blue sky. Tim and his friends loved their fun day with the pears and the ball.

And from that day on, every time Tim and his friends played together, they would always remember the big pear tree and the quiet, happy day they spent under it.

Mia's friend, Tim, came to visit her. He saw that Mia was sad and asked, "Mia, why are you sad?" Mia told Tim, "I can't find my fancy flute. I want to play music, but I can't." Tim wanted to help Mia, so they started to look for the fancy flute together.

They looked in the house, under the bed, and in the yard, but they could not find the fancy flute. Then, Tim had an idea. "Mia, did you look in your toy box?" Mia shook her head. They went to the toy box and started to look. At the bottom of the box, they found the fancy flute! Mia was so happy to get her flute back. Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a little boy named Tim. Tim was a good boy who liked to listen to his mom and dad. One day, it was very hot outside, so Tim's mom said, "Tim, please stay inside today. It is too hot to play outside."

Tim listened to his mom and stayed inside. He played with his toys and read his books. As he was playing, he heard an alarm coming from the kitchen. Tim ran to see what was happening. His mom was cooking, and the alarm was telling her that the food was ready. "Mom, what is that noise?" Tim asked. His mom said, "That is the alarm, Tim. It tells me when the food is cooked."

Tim was curious about the alarm, so he asked his mom if he could listen to it again. His mom agreed and showed him how the alarm worked. She said, "Tim, remember to always listen to the alarm. It can help keep us safe."

Later that day, Tim and his mom went to the store. As they were shopping, they heard an alarm. Tim remembered what his mom said and knew that they needed to listen to the alarm. They quickly left the store, and it turned out there was a small fire in the back. Because they listened to the alarm, they were safe.

The moral of the story is to always listen to alarms and to the people who care for you. They can help keep you safe and happy.

Remy wanted to help the blue bird. He thought for a moment and said, "I can't fly, but I have an idea. Let's ask my friend, the wise owl. He can help you understand how to fly."

The blue bird tried to do what the owl said. It flapped its wings fast and jumped. The bird started to fly! The blue bird was so happy and said, "Thank you, Remy and wise owl! Now I understand how to fly!"

"Yum, this cake is so delicious!" said Lily. "Who put it here?" Just then, they heard a voice. "I did," said a friendly old man. "I knew you kids would find it. I put it here for you to enjoy."

Lily and her friends thanked the old man and rode back home, feeling happy and full. From that day on, they always remembered the delicious cake they found underground.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a diary where she wrote all her secrets and feelings. One day, Lily's friend, Tommy, came to play. Tommy saw the diary and wanted to read it. 

Lily said, "No, Tommy. That's my diary. It's kind of you to ask, but it's private." 

Tommy paused and thought about what Lily said. He realized that he wouldn't want someone to read his diary either. 

"I'm sorry, Lily. You're right. It's important to be kind and respect other people's things," said Tommy. 

Lily smiled and said, "It's okay, Tommy. I forgive you. Let's play together instead." 

The moral of the story is that it's important to be kind and respect other people's things, even if we're curious.

Together, Jack and Sarah wrapped the present with pretty paper and a bow. Jack was very happy with how it looked. He said, "Thank you for your help, Sarah. Lily will love it!" Sarah smiled and said, "I'm happy to help. Bye-bye, Jack!" Jack waved goodbye and sailed away on his gray boat.

The worm thought and thought about how he could get the apple. Suddenly, he saw a big leaf on the ground. He thought he could use it to climb the tree. So, he crawled onto the leaf and started to climb. But as he climbed, the leaf slipped and he fell down to the ground.

The worm was sad and frustrated. But then he had an idea. He crawled over to a group of ants and asked for their help. The ants were happy to help and together they climbed up the tree and got the apple. The worm was so happy and grateful that he shared the apple with all the ants. Tom and Anna see a man who works at the park. He is wearing a blue shirt and a hat. He is feeding the fish.

"Excuse me, sir. What is oxygen?" Tom asks.

The man smiles and kneels down to talk to Tom and Anna.

"Oxygen is a very important thing, kids. It is in the air we breathe. It helps us live and talk. The fish also need oxygen, but they get it from the water. The water has oxygen too, but not as much as the air. That's why the fish tank has a machine that makes bubbles. The bubbles give more oxygen to the water and the fish." The man explains.

"Wow, that is very interesting. Thank you, sir." Tom says.

"Yes, thank you. You are very smart." Anna says.

The man laughs and says, "You are very welcome, kids. You are very curious and polite. I'm glad you like the fish. They are very beautiful and special. But remember, they are also very poor. They cannot leave the fish tank. They cannot see the sky or the trees or the flowers. They cannot play with other animals. They only have each other. So we have to be kind and respectful to them. We have to take care of them and their oxygen. Okay?"

"Okay, sir. We understand. We will be kind and respectful to the fish. We will not touch them or make noise or throw things at them. We will just watch them and learn from them." Tom and Anna say.

"Good. That's very nice of you. I'm sure the fish appreciate it. Now, have fun and enjoy the park. But don't forget to breathe. Oxygen is good for you too." The man says.

Tom and Anna wave goodbye to the man and the fish. They go to play on the swings and the slide. They breathe the fresh air and feel happy. They have learned something new today. They have learned about oxygen.

The doctor said, "Lily, I need to see inside your arm. I have a special machine that can do that. It is called an x-ray. It will not hurt you, I promise. But you need to be very still and let me take a picture of your arm. Can you do that?"

Lily nodded. She was scared, but she wanted her arm to feel better. Mom held her hand and said, "You are very brave, Lily. I am proud of you."

The doctor put Lily's arm on a table and covered it with a soft cloth. Then he moved a big machine over her arm. It made a funny noise. Lily closed her eyes and did not move.

The doctor said, "All done, Lily. You did great. Let me show you the picture of your arm." He took a paper from the machine and showed it to Lily and Mom. It had a black and white image of Lily's arm, with bones and shapes.

The doctor said, "See, Lily, this is your arm. And this is where it is broken. You need a cast to help it heal. A cast is a hard bandage that will keep your arm in place. You can choose the color you like. And you can have your friends sign it and draw on it. How does that sound?"

Lily smiled. She liked the idea of a cast. She said, "Can I have a pink cast, please?"

The doctor said, "Of course, Lily. Pink is a lovely color. Let me get it for you." He went to get the cast and came back with a roll of pink material. He wrapped it around Lily's arm and made it smooth and hard.

Lily looked at her arm and said, "Wow, it looks cool. Thank you, doctor."

The doctor said, "You are very welcome, Lily. You are a strong and brave girl. Now you need to rest and take care of your arm. And you can show it to your friends and family. They will love it."

Lily hugged Mom and said, "Thank you, Mom. I love you."

Mom said, "I love you too, Lily. You are my sweet girl." They left the doctor's office and went home. Lily felt better and was happy with her pink cast.

"Look, Mom, the hippo is spraying water!" Tim said, pointing at the hippo. The hippo was using his nose to blow water in the air, like a fountain. It made a funny sound, and the water fell on the other hippos and the grass.

"Wow, that's cool!" Jen said. She wanted to spray water too. She saw a hose near the fence, and ran to it. She turned on the tap, and held the hose. She aimed at the hippo, and squeezed the handle.

"Jen, no!" Mom shouted. "That's not nice! You can't spray the hippo!"

But it was too late. Jen sprayed the hippo with the hose, and the hippo did not like it. He roared and opened his mouth, showing his big teeth. He sprayed water back at Jen, and hit her in the face. Jen dropped the hose and screamed. She was wet and scared.

"Jen, I'm sorry, I'm sorry!" Tim said, running to her. He hugged her and tried to calm her down. He felt bad for her and the hippo.

"Jen, that was a bad thing to do," Dad said, picking her up. "You should never spray the animals. They have feelings too, and they don't like to be bothered."

"I'm sorry, Dad," Jen said, sobbing. "I just wanted to have fun. I didn't mean to make the hippo angry."

"It's okay, Jen," Mom said, wiping her face. "You made a mistake, but you learned from it. Next time, you can watch the hippo spray, but not spray him yourself."

Just when Lily was about to scream for help, her friends found her. They quickly opened the drawer and helped her out. Lily was so happy to be out of the cabinet that she decided to bury it in the backyard. From that day on, Lily never played hide and seek in her cabinet again.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went on a walk in the forest with his mommy. They saw a big mountain far away. Timmy said, "Mommy, I want to climb the mountain!" His mommy said, "No, Timmy, it's too dangerous."

Suddenly, they saw smoke coming from the mountain. Timmy said, "Mommy, what's happening to the mountain?" His mommy said, "Oh no, the mountain is burning! We have to go back home now."

When they got home, Timmy felt sad and ashamed. He said, "Mommy, I'm sorry for wanting to climb the mountain. I didn't know it would burn." His mommy hugged him and said, "It's okay, Timmy. We all make mistakes. The important thing is that we learn from them."

The fake pilot wanted to take Timmy's toy airplane away. Timmy didn't want to give it up, so he hid it in his room. But the fake pilot kept peeking in his window, trying to find it. 

Timmy was scared and didn't know what to do. But then he had an idea. He put a note on his toy airplane that said "Property of Timmy, not for fake pilots." The fake pilot saw the note and left Timmy alone. Timmy was happy he didn't have to give up his toy airplane and could keep pretending to be a pilot. The end.

Together, they lifted the hammer and built a beautiful home for the ant. The ant was very happy and grateful. The bee had offered help when the ant needed it most. And now, they were the best of friends.

Lily's mom told her that if she was good, she could have a surprise later. Lily was so happy and promised to behave. Later that day, they went back to the playground and Lily saw a new swing. It was big and shiny and looked like so much fun. She ran to it and started swinging higher and higher. Suddenly, her mom called out "surprise!" and handed her the toy car. Lily was so happy and felt like the luckiest girl in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her favorite doll named Rosie. One day, Lily's little brother came into her room and took Rosie away from her. Lily felt very sad and didn't know what to do.

Then, their mom came into the room and saw that Lily was crying. She asked what was wrong and Lily told her that her brother took Rosie away. The mom said she would help and went to find Lily's brother. She asked him to remove Rosie from his hands and give her back to Lily.

The brother listened to their mom and gave Rosie back to Lily. She was so happy and hugged Rosie tightly. The nurse who was taking care of their mom came into the room and saw Lily laughing. She said that Lily was so funny and made everyone smile. From then on, Lily made sure to keep her toys close and her brother learned to share.

Once upon a time, there was a tall duck who liked to swim in the pond. He was happy and quacked loudly. One day, a hunter came to the pond with a gun. He wanted to shoot the duck. The poor duck didn't know what was happening and continued to swim. Suddenly, the hunter shot the duck and he fell to the ground. The other ducks were sad and they quacked quietly. The hunter took the duck away and the pond was never the same again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his tools, especially his hammer. He would use it to build all sorts of things, like forts and toy cars.

One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy wanted to play with Timmy's hammer, but Timmy didn't want to share it. "No, Billy. This is my tool. I don't want to give it to you," said Timmy.

Billy was sad and went home. Later that day, Timmy's dad came home from work and saw Timmy playing with his hammer. "Wow, Timmy! You're doing a great job. I'm so proud of you for using your tool to build something amazing," said Timmy's dad.

Timmy felt happy and proud. He realized that sharing his tool with Billy would have been a nice thing to do. The next day, when Billy came over to play, Timmy offered to share his hammer. Billy was happy and they played together, displaying their creations proudly.

Once upon a time, there was a little gray kitten named Mittens. Mittens loved to play and explore, but one day she got stuck on a tall stage. She meowed and meowed, but nobody heard her.

Just when Mittens thought she would be stuck forever, a friendly dog named Max came to the rescue. Max barked and jumped until he knocked down the stage and freed Mittens.

From that day on, Mittens and Max became the best of friends. Mittens would curl up on Max's warm belly and they would nap together. Mittens was so grateful to Max for rescuing her from the stage that she would lick his face and purr every time she saw him.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He had two thumbs, one on each hand. But his left thumb was different from his right thumb. 

One day, Timmy and his friends played a game. They had to throw a ball into a basket. The first one to get three balls in the basket would win. Timmy tried and tried, but he couldn't get any balls in the basket. 

But then, on his last try, he threw the ball and it went straight into the basket! Timmy won the game and his friends cheered for him. He was so happy that he jumped up and down and showed his different thumbs to everyone.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit named Bouncy. Bouncy loved to jump high and far. He was very good at it. One day, Bouncy met a mouse named Squeaky. Squeaky had a nice tooth necklace. Bouncy wanted the necklace, so he asked Squeaky if he could have it. Squeaky said no because the necklace was very special to him.

Bouncy didn't like that answer, so he decided to take the necklace from Squeaky. He jumped at Squeaky and knocked him over. But when Bouncy picked up the necklace, he realized that he had hurt Squeaky. Bouncy felt very bad and gave the necklace back to Squeaky. Bouncy learned that it's not nice to take things from others and that it's important to be kind and respectful. From that day on, Bouncy made sure to use his jumping skills to help others and make them happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear who lived in a cozy cave. Every day, he would go outside to play in the forest. One day, he found a shiny rock that he really liked. He wanted to measure it to see how big it was. He took out his ruler and measured the rock. It was a fair size, not too big and not too small.

The bear was very happy with his new rock. He wanted to show it off to his friends. He invited them over to his cave for a luxury tea party. They all had a great time drinking tea and eating cookies. The bear showed his friends his new rock and they were all very impressed. They thought it was a luxury rock because it was so shiny and pretty.

After the tea party, the bear and his friends went back outside to play. They decided to have a race to see who was the fastest. The bear won the race because he was the biggest and strongest. He was very proud of himself and his new rock. From that day on, the bear always carried his rock with him wherever he went.

Once upon a time, there was a fish named Fin. Fin lived in a big, blue ocean with his fish friends. One day, Fin saw a long hook in the water. He knew it was dangerous, so he swam away fast. But one of his friends got stuck on the hook! Fin wanted to help his friend escape. He swam over to the hook and bit it with his sharp teeth. The hook came loose and his friend was free! Fin felt happy that he could help his friend. From then on, Fin and his friends were more careful of the long hooks in the water.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went outside to play in the rain. She loved to jump in the puddles and feel the wet drops on her face. Suddenly, her mom called her on the telephone. 

"Hi, Mommy!" Lily said, picking up the phone. 

"Hi, sweetie," her mom replied. "I just wanted to mention that it's getting late. It's time to come inside and get dry." 

Lily was sad to leave her fun in the rain, but she knew her mom was right. She said goodbye to her friends outside and went inside to change into warm, dry clothes. As she snuggled up with a blanket, she remembered how much fun she had playing in the rain and couldn't wait to do it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, her mommy said, "Lily, let's go to the post office to get some stamps." Lily was excited because she had never been to the post office before. 

At the post office, Lily saw a big machine that allowed people to buy stamps. Her mommy gave her some money to put in the machine, and it gave her a stamp. Lily was so happy to have her very own stamp. 

After they left the post office, Lily saw a tall tree with branches that went really high. She asked her mommy if she could climb the tree, but her mommy said it was too dangerous. Lily was sad, but her mommy explained that it was important to be safe. 

Lily learned that sometimes we can't do everything we want, but it's okay because there are things that we are allowed to do, like buy stamps at the post office.

Once upon a time, there was a family who lived in a house with a big carpet. The family had a brother and a sister who liked to play together. One day, they started to quarrel over a toy car. The brother wanted to play with it, but the sister didn't want to share.

The sister got angry and threw the toy car on the carpet. The brother got mad and pushed the sister. She fell and hit her head on the carpet. At first, it seemed harmless, but soon she started to feel sick. The family took her to the hospital, but it was too late. The sister had a serious injury and could not be saved.

The family was very sad and regretted the quarrel. They learned that it's important to share and not fight over things. They also learned that even harmless things can be dangerous if we don't take care. From that day on, they always remembered their sister and the lesson they learned.

Once upon a time, there was a big gorilla in the jungle. He was very strong and had thick fur. One day, he went to the store to buy bananas. But when he got there, he saw that all the bananas were gone. He was very sad and angry because he loved bananas.

The gorilla asked the store worker where the bananas were. The worker said that they were all sold out. The gorilla didn't like that answer. He started to bang on the walls and throw things around. The store worker was scared and called for help.

Soon, some other animals came to the store to help calm the gorilla down. They brought him some other fruits to eat instead of bananas. The gorilla was still upset, but he was happy to have something to eat. From that day on, he learned to store some extra bananas at home so he would never run out again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to the park with her mommy and daddy. At the park, there was a big gate that opened and closed. Lily liked to watch the gate go up and down. She said, "I can do that too!" and tried to push the gate. But it was too heavy for her.

After playing on the swings and slide, Lily felt uncomfortable. She had sand in her shoes and her clothes were dirty. So, her mommy and daddy helped her clean up and put on fresh clothes. Then, they went home and had a yummy snack. Lily was happy and tired from all the fun she had at the park.

Once upon a time, there was an old motor. It was very tired and didn't work well. One day, a little boy wanted to play with the motor. He tried to make it work, but it wouldn't start. He felt sad and frustrated.

Then, the boy had an idea. He took a step back and looked at the motor. He saw that it was very dirty and had lots of dust on it. So, he got a cloth and cleaned the motor. After he cleaned it, the motor started to work again! The boy was so happy and excited.

But then, his little sister wanted to play with the motor too. They both wanted to play with it at the same time. They started to argue and fight over who could play with the motor. The boy remembered what he did before and took another step back. He thought about how he could solve the problem. Finally, he suggested that they take turns playing with the motor. They both agreed and were happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Max. Max had a long tail that he loved to wag when he was happy. One day, Max went on an adventure to find some cheese. He walked and walked until he came across a big wall. Max tried to climb the wall, but it was too difficult for him. 

Just then, a friendly bird named Bella flew by. "Hi Max! What are you doing?" asked Bella. "I'm trying to reach the cheese on the other side of this wall, but it's too difficult for me," replied Max. "I can help you!" said Bella. 

Bella flew over the wall and brought back some cheese for Max. Max was so happy and grateful. "Thank you, Bella! You have a very kind heart," said Max, wagging his tail happily. From that day on, Max and Bella became good friends and went on many more adventures together.
